- We value transparency, the willingness to try a bunch of things and learn from them, and be challenged by different ideas

- We believe crowdfunding is a new way for creators to bring their projects to life, or even help jumpstart their dream of starting their own business

- BackerKit is a profitable company, and have received funding from YC and SVAngel

You:

- You have spent time working on a fairly large Rails app

- You understand and has empathy for the culture of creators and backers in the crowdfunding space and bottom-up economy

- You have rare people skills which allow you to get out in front of problems and proactively help customers with potential troubles

- You love working one-on-one with customers in helping them succeed

- You are hungry to learn and move fast, and can buckle down to get things done

- You are passionate, creative, have other interests, and work on other projects - You are also great at communicating clearly to team members often about ideas, issues, or improvements

- You are conscious of your current level of productivity and happiness, and make continual changes to grow

- You are excited to work with a small team

- You are someone who is a pleasure to work with and encourages the entire team to improve their craft

- You are not afraid to get your hands dirty and do some good old-fashioned schlepping

- You are entrepreneurial - we trust everyone on our team to make bold choices and do what is best to grow the company

Primary Responsibilities:

- Talking to customers via email and occasionally phone about improvements or issues they may be having

- Lead a small but growing team of developers

- Make important technical decisions that have sweeping consequences for our customers and the business

- Release early and often

- Product input. We are a small team who moves fast, so it is important that you speak you mind and give feedback on how we can make things better/faster/stronger

- Talk to users. Everyone at BackerKit is customer-facing, and we expect everyone to get to know the project creators we are serving (plus, they are awesome, just like you)

If this sounds like a team you’d like to be a part of, please email maxwell@backerkit.com with your resume and/or Github.

Extra credit: Send us over a list of URLs to any Kickstarter, Indiegogo, Tilt, or other crowdfunded campaigns you’ve supported.

Look forward to helping creators together!

One Month (YC S13) Is Looking for Amazing Teachers – JavaScript, Python, UX
Clever (YC S12) is looking for full-stack engineers – help change the classroom
text:
There’s a lot of great educational software out there - think Oregon Trail, Math Blasters, and Carmen Sandiego - but teachers can’t use it in schools. Teachers would love to use programs like these, but synchronizing data between their school’s database and external software applications is a huge problem that results in wasted time at the start of class and frustrated, bored students… which leads to software being abandoned entirely. 80% of K-12 teachers would use more software in classes if getting students logged in weren’t such a hassle, and a quarter of all class time that’s supposed to be dedicated to software is wasted on logins alone.

Developers have a similar problem: they love clean APIs, but in the education industry, they haven’t had one. Most K-12 schools house their student data in ancient legacy databases that make integrations a nightmare. If you’re a five-person startup and you’ve built an app that revolutionizes the way third-graders learn fractions, there’s simply no way to get your product in front of students.

Clever (YC S12 - clever.com) is solving these problems by building a modern, developer-friendly API for schools… which we give them for free. Developers love being able to plug into schools without having to write a complex integration for every single district they’re working with, so they pay us for access to the platform. This business model has helped us grow quickly; we’re now in 1 in 5 schools in America (over 29,000 schools), and our product is used by millions of students every day.

Our goal is to become the education identity company. The first step in that direction is our Instant Login single sign-on platform: a universal login that allows students to access all of their learning applications in one place. (This is a big deal if you’ve ever seen a second-grader try to manage fifteen different usernames and passwords.)

Right now we’re a team of 35 people (17 engineers) based in downtown San Francisco. We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

Other stuff we like: -Tech talks. Every other Tuesday, we do “Clever Talks” during lunch where one of us will give a presentation on anything he/she’s interested in. Recent talks have covered exoplanets, neuroscience, hacking big-company customer service interactions, and what’s wrong with American high school history education. -Bughouse chess. We play pretty frequently, although not always with Magnus Carlsen: http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo -Picking up new skills. We offer unlimited Amazon credits for learning.

Check us out: https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

title: Join Clara Labs (YC S14) – Help Machines Cheat on the Turing Test
text:
-What we're doing-

Clara Labs is building the first artificially intelligent employee. For the past nine months, we've built a system that supplements machine intelligence with human contextual awareness to support our first task: scheduling meetings. Clara already handles complex email-based coordination and scheduling for executives, recruiters, and sales teams at companies like Stripe, ZenPayroll, Heroku, Mattermark, and AngelList.

-How we're doing it-

Our software distributes the most complex natural language processing questions to human contractors, while automating the parts of the work a machine can grapple with on its own. This human-machine combination works well, but also presents some interesting challenges:

1. Reliability: How do you architect a distributed human-machine system whose reliability must be very high?

2. Interaction: The foundational relationship between humans and AI is yet to be designed; how do you establish a virtual relationship that feels intimate and natural?

3. Operations: How do you build the infrastructure to manage a distributed workforce of thousands?

-Who we are-

We're a small team working from the Mission in San Francisco. We like productive debate, reading (especially about intelligence), and care deeply about creating truly great products.

-What we're looking for-

We care about authenticity, thoughtfulness, and work ethic. We're looking for early team members to help us build the core of the company - engineering, operations, design, sales, and support.

Interested in learning more? Send us a note at join@claralabs.com!

text:
WePay is looking for talented and motivated software engineers to join our rapidly expanding team. Our transaction volume has more than tripled year-over-year and we’re rapidly outgrowing our existing tech stack. We’re working to rebuild our application on top of a brand new service-oriented architecture and need your help. Do you love programming, take pride in the quality of your code, and are at least decent at ping pong? We want to talk to you!

* You have to be a great coder. We’re working with real money so writing efficient, maintainable and well tested code is a must. * You must be open-minded, flexible, and have a pragmatic approach to solving problems. The payments industry can be baffling at times, so we value people who can persevere and continue to make progress with a positive attitude.

One or more of the following skills would be awesome:

* Front-end expertise including: HTML5, JavaScript, CSS, AngularJS

* Back-end expertise with RDBMS and NOSQL databases, messaging and queuing systems, batch and scheduled tasks

* Restful API design and implementation

* Building highly available and distributed systems

* Big Data experience including Hadoop, Storm, Kafka, etc.

* Machine Learning and Modeling

* Experience in Risk and Fraud Detection

* Experience in payments and PCI compliance

Clever (YC S12) is looking for full-stack engineers – help change the classroom
text:
There’s a lot of great educational software out there - think Oregon Trail, Math Blasters, and Carmen Sandiego - but teachers can’t use it in schools. Teachers would love to use programs like these, but synchronizing data between their school’s database and external software applications is a huge problem that results in wasted time at the start of class and frustrated, bored students… which leads to software being abandoned entirely. 80% of K-12 teachers would use more software in classes if getting students logged in weren’t such a hassle, and a quarter of all class time that’s supposed to be dedicated to software is wasted on logins alone.

Developers have a similar problem: they love clean APIs, but in the education industry, they haven’t had one. Most K-12 schools house their student data in ancient legacy databases that make integrations a nightmare. If you’re a five-person startup and you’ve built an app that revolutionizes the way third-graders learn fractions, there’s simply no way to get your product in front of students.

Clever (YC S12 - clever.com) is solving these problems by building a modern, developer-friendly API for schools… which we give them for free. Developers love being able to plug into schools without having to write a complex integration for every single district they’re working with, so they pay us for access to the platform. This business model has helped us grow quickly; we’re now in 1 in 5 schools in America (over 29,000 schools), and our product is used by millions of students every day.

Our goal is to become the education identity company. The first step in that direction is our Instant Login single sign-on platform: a universal login that allows students to access all of their learning applications in one place. (This is a big deal if you’ve ever seen a second-grader try to manage fifteen different usernames and passwords.)

Right now we’re a team of 35 people (17 engineers) based in downtown San Francisco. We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

Other stuff we like: -Tech talks. Every other Tuesday, we do “Clever Talks” during lunch where one of us will give a presentation on anything he/she’s interested in. Recent talks have covered exoplanets, neuroscience, hacking big-company customer service interactions, and what’s wrong with American high school history education. -Bughouse chess. We play pretty frequently, although not always with Magnus Carlsen: http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo -Picking up new skills. We offer unlimited Amazon credits for learning.

Check us out: https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

text:
What we're doing

Clara Labs is building the first artificially intelligent employee. For the past nine months, we've built a system that supplements machine intelligence with human contextual awareness to support our first task: scheduling meetings. Clara already handles complex email-based coordination and scheduling for executives, recruiters, and sales teams at companies like Stripe, ZenPayroll, Heroku, Mattermark, and AngelList.

How we're doing it

Our software distributes the most complex natural language processing questions to human contractors, while automating the parts of the work a machine can grapple with on its own. This human-machine combination works well, but also presents some interesting challenges:

1. Reliability: How do you architect a distributed human-machine system whose reliability must be very high?

2. Interaction: The foundational relationship between humans and AI is yet to be designed; how do you establish a virtual relationship that feels intimate and natural?

3. Operations: How do you build the infrastructure to manage a distributed workforce of thousands?

Who we are

We're a small team working from the Mission in San Francisco. We like productive debate, reading (especially about intelligence), and care deeply about creating truly great products.

What we're looking for

We care about authenticity, thoughtfulness, and work ethic. We're looking for early team members to help us build the core of the company - engineering, operations, design, sales, and support.

Interested in learning more? Send us a note at team@claralabs.com!

VERBLING OVERVIEW

Verbling is a San Francisco startup helping the world learn foreign languages. Students on six continents use Verbling to realize their dreams. We're looking for amazing people to make more dreams come true.

At Verbling, we see the faces of our users every single day. They're more than numbers on a graph. Language students fumble with grammar, learn slang, and laugh in live Verbling classes 24/7. We're targeting over a billion language learners previously locked into a dead, broken market, now ripe for disruption thanks to technology.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

The first ten team members shape the company's culture, a culture that will mean everything as the organization scales. Therefore, we look for those with founder mentality. We want to bring on board people who take initiative, who aren't afraid of responsibility, and who understand the inherent value in moving fast and taking risks.

San Francisco - Full-time

Javascript is crucial to Verbling. We use Node.js on the backend and a Backbone-based framework on the front-end. We are looking for someone who's excited about getting their hands dirty in all part of the stack.

You are a experienced Javascript developer who wants to get in on building the future of ed-tech from the bottom up. You want to be an integral part in inventing new ways for students to learn foreign languages.

You love to learn, and equally love to share your knowledge with others. You’re both a listener and contributor. You are a great communicator and you take care to understand before making yourself understood.

Your code is architected for scalability, re-use, and testability. Your operators are always === and you are a master of closures. You have strong opinions on code structure and modularization. You're pretty darn excited about isometric flux, generators, and FRP.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Own and drive projects from idea spec to production. Work closely with product and design teams. Continually iterate on product features using analytics and user feedback.

REQUIREMENTS

Experience with Node.js. Experience in front-end JS development, and preferably in a framework like Backbone, Angular, etc. Always thinking about scalability and performance bottlenecks. A test-driven mindset.

BONUS

Interest in spoken languages. Open-source contributions. Experience in NoSQL; MongoDB, Couch, redis, or similar.

title: Classrooms look the same way they did in 1960. Help fix that at Clever (YC S12)
text:
There’s a lot of great educational software out there - think Oregon Trail, Math Blasters, and Carmen Sandiego - but teachers can’t use it in schools. Teachers would love to use programs like these, but synchronizing data between their school’s database and external software applications is a huge problem that results in wasted time at the start of class and frustrated, bored students… which leads to software being abandoned entirely. 80% of K-12 teachers would use more software in classes if getting students logged in weren’t such a hassle, and a quarter of all class time that’s supposed to be dedicated to software is wasted on logins alone.

Developers have a similar problem: they love clean APIs, but in the education industry, they haven’t had one. Most K-12 schools house their student data in ancient legacy databases that make integrations a nightmare. If you’re a five-person startup and you’ve built an app that revolutionizes the way third-graders learn fractions, there’s simply no way to get your product in front of students.

Clever (YC S12 - clever.com) is solving these problems by building a modern, developer-friendly API for schools… which we give them for free. Developers love being able to plug into schools without having to write a complex integration for every single district they’re working with, so they pay us for access to the platform. This business model has helped us grow quickly; we’re now in 1 in 5 schools in America (over 29,000 schools), and our product is used by millions of students every day.

Our goal is to become the education identity company. The first step in that direction is our Instant Login single sign-on platform: a universal login that allows students to access all of their learning applications in one place. (This is a big deal if you’ve ever seen a second-grader try to manage fifteen different usernames and passwords.)

Right now we’re a team of 35 people (17 engineers) based in downtown San Francisco. We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

Other stuff we like: -Tech talks. Every other Tuesday, we do “Clever Talks” during lunch where one of us will give a presentation on anything he/she’s interested in. Recent talks have covered exoplanets, neuroscience, hacking big-company customer service interactions, and what’s wrong with American high school history education. -Bughouse chess. We play pretty frequently, although not always with Magnus Carlsen: http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo -Picking up new skills. We offer unlimited Amazon credits for learning.

Check us out: https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

title: Classrooms look the same way they did in 1960. Help fix that at Clever (YC S12)
text:
There’s a lot of great educational software out there - think Oregon Trail, Math Blasters, and Carmen Sandiego - but teachers can’t use it in schools. Teachers would love to use programs like these, but synchronizing data between their school’s database and external software applications is a huge problem that results in wasted time at the start of class and frustrated, bored students… which leads to software being abandoned entirely. 80% of K-12 teachers would use more software in classes if getting students logged in weren’t such a hassle, and a quarter of all class time that’s supposed to be dedicated to software is wasted on logins alone.

Developers have a similar problem: they love clean APIs, but in the education industry, they haven’t had one. Most K-12 schools house their student data in ancient legacy databases that make integrations a nightmare. If you’re a five-person startup and you’ve built an app that revolutionizes the way third-graders learn fractions, there’s simply no way to get your product in front of students.

Clever (YC S12 - clever.com) is solving these problems by building a modern, developer-friendly API for schools… which we give them for free. Developers love being able to plug into schools without having to write a complex integration for every single district they’re working with, so they pay us for access to the platform. This business model has helped us grow quickly; we’re now in 1 in 5 schools in America (over 29,000 schools), and our product is used by millions of students every day. It's also great to hear positive feedback from teachers and administrators who are finally able to use the software tools they've always wanted in class.

Our goal is to become the education identity company. The first step in that direction is our Instant Login single sign-on platform: a universal login that allows students to access all of their learning applications in one place. (This is a big deal if you’ve ever seen a second-grader try to manage fifteen different usernames and passwords.)

Right now we’re a team of 35 people (17 engineers) based in downtown San Francisco. We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

Other stuff we like: -Tech talks. Every other Tuesday, we do “Clever Talks” during lunch where one of us will give a presentation on anything he/she’s interested in. Recent talks have covered exoplanets, neuroscience, hacking big-company customer service interactions, and what’s wrong with American high school history education. -Bughouse chess. We play pretty frequently, although not always with Magnus Carlsen: http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo -Picking up new skills. We offer unlimited Amazon credits for learning.

Check us out: https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

title: Build our content marketing strategy from the ground up – 42Floors
Content and Social Media Marketing Intern
text:
We're an off-the-record YC company that's fresh out of the winter '14 batch and growing fast. Everyday our clients call and email to say that we're making them happy. And that feels great.

We are looking to hire a content and social media marketing intern to conduct research, write a few blog posts per week, manage and grow our social media community, write and promote press-releases, and help with various other marketing initiatives.

Come learn about the way a fast-growing startup works and use your creativity and passion for writing and marketing to help us build this company. Work with a down-to-earth, smart, and experienced start up team who will offer enough guidance to help you succeed and enough autonomy to have a real sense of ownership. Build your digital marketing skills and help us continue to accelerate our growth.

We're looking for people who are curious, and clear communicators. People who love digging into complicated or intimidating subjects, and pulling out the important, urgent issues at their core, because what we're doing is important, and it is urgent. We're attacking a wasteful, insecure part of the home-buying process that costs Americans $50 billion a year, often causes them enormous stress, and sometimes exposes them to scary things like identity theft. Help us change an enormous and antiquated industry to make home buying better for consumers.

Responsibilities specifically include:

* Writing blog posts that are informative and human, useful both in- and outside of our company (this means technical content written in fluid prose) Communicating with influencers in our industry, writing press releases, and pushing them to different PR channels Building our community on social media, helping us spread the word about the important work we are doing and establishing our voice within our industry * Other various and sundry marketing initiatives from SEO to event planning and more

What we're looking for:

* Someone who can write clearly and persuasively * Have some experience with social media (ideally for a business or startup) * Be detail-oriented (with nicely organized details to prove it) * Eager and driven (while still courteous) * Experience with real estate or mortgage is a HUGE plus (but not required) * Someone who can work 10-20 hours a week, (in our San Francisco office and from home) * This is paid (by the hour) * Students welcome - turn this into a work-study project and have a clear mentor within the organization

Send us an email to fintechw14@gmail.com telling us about yourself. Please include a resume and writing samples.

title: MakeSchool, a.k.a MakeGamesWithUs, Is Looking for a Rails Dev and Instructor
How often does a K-12 teacher thank you for coding? Find out at Clever (YC S12)
text:
Steve Jobs described education as one of the final frontiers still untouched by modern technology. Clever (YC S12 - https://clever.com) is building the data platform needed for great software to make its way into the classroom. Just like Stripe has made it simple for developers to build payment processing into their apps, Clever has made it easy for developers to build applications for schools using student data.

We're a small, highly technical team (35 people, 17 engineers) with deep experience in education. In under two years, 1 in 5 schools in America has begun using our APIs, meaning that Clever moves data for eight million students every day.

Our newest project is essentially Facebook Connect for education: one identity to tie together all of a student’s learning applications into a cohesive experience. We’re making that happen with our Instant Login service, which allows students to log in once and immediately get access to all their apps: https://www.edsurge.com/n/2014-05-14-no-more-passwords-cleve...

And while we have all the startup perks (a beautiful loft office in SoMa, free lunch, unlimited Amazon credits for learning..) – hands down the best part of the job are the calls and emails from schools describing how much Clever helps them.

As an education company, we’re all about learning personally too – it’s practically a prerequisite to work here. In the past few weeks we’ve done tech talks on things like exoplanets, set theory, and kitesurfing. (We also love a good round of bughouse chess – just ask Magnus Carlsen http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo)

We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

Nice-to-haves:

MakeSchool aka MakeGamesWithUs is hiring a Rails developer, instructor
text:
MakeSchool is looking for a rails developer to teach the web development portion of our new gap year program (http://www.makeschool.com). You'll be teaching students aged ~18-25 how to build and ship their first website! Our curriculum will cover Ruby on Rails and HTML/CSS/JS, you'll get to heavily influence the curriculum for this year and the future. You'll also get to help guide the students' product ideas, help them understand how to effectively code on a team and prepare them to become professional developers or startup founders. Our students are some of the brightest in the nation, they've been coding for years, have already shipped iOS games and apps and have a passion for building great products. It's an exciting opportunity to help inspire the next generation of makers and help define the future of CS education.

What we’re looking for: - Passion for teaching and teaching experience - Strong CS background and industry experience building real products - Significant experience with RoR/HTML/CSS/JS (bonus for having scaled a rails app)

The position would start mid-november at the latest, we'd be happy to have you start right away to help develop the curriculum. The teaching period will last 3 months, after which you would contribute to curriculum development, website development and a variety of other areas. Our team cares deeply about the problems in education we are trying to solve, and we'd love if you do too. We're a tight knit group of 8, our team has moved from Hawaii, Michigan, Germany and Boston to join us. It's a diverse, fast paced and fun environment.

Interested? Contact ashu@makegameswith.us

--

About Us: MakeSchool is building a replacement for the computer science degree. This summer we taught 120 high school and college students how to build iOS apps across SF, Palo Alto and NYC. We're currently piloting a 1 year college supplement where students learn mobile and web development, computer science theory, and development focused career skills. The year culminates with an internship at a tech startup. The next step is a 2 year college replacement that will prepare students for a career as a founder or developer. We're looking to build the college experience we wished existed. Our curriculum is used to teach courses at 3 of the top 4 universities for computer engineering. Over 300 students have taken our in-person courses and over half a million students have used our online tutorials. We were founded in 2012 and are funded by Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, Alexis Ohanian, Tim Draper and more.

title: iOS and Web Developers Wanted. Let's Clean Up the Telecoms Industry
text:
Join us in building a new kind of phone company and fight against the Telco monopolies.

If you're interested, please drop us a line: jobs [at] sendhub [dot] com

About SendHub: We're building tools to make it fast and easy for businesses to communicate with their customers and employees.

Founded to help educators in under resourced communities, we’re taking on the Telecom giants. Hate your phone carrier? Us too. Telecommunications is a duopoly dominated industry, which has systematically suppressed competition over its 150 year history, in order to keep prices unfairly high. We’re going to change this, starting with business phone service. We have a ~$1M annual run rate and have raised ~$10M.

We’re looking for talented engineers with a strong sense of ownership to lead our iOS/Web efforts. We want you to take our apps to the next level; building communication features that are immersive, reliable, and performant.

The Role: You’ll be in charge of building out our next generation voice & messaging app (Web or iOS). Responsibilities include building features, fixing bugs, and collaborating with our technically skilled design team to deliver the best possible end-user experience. title: Build a bank
text:
We’re in a new era of banking...and it demands a new, full stack, approach to wholesale and commercial banking. A software first approach, not a people first approach.

Why?

Because we've learned a lot about banks and we've walked away shocked at the state of their technology, their culture, their "innovations", their complacency...and the potential to do better.

We're building a bank that focuses on slightly different things than other banks. Focused on building a great product, a great platform, and a great experience. Banks legacy limitations make it hard to run a technology business with a financial component. It limits the potential of products. It makes the world a worse place.

We're putting APIs, developer tools, automated fraud detection, and data at the center of our product offerings and security, distributed systems, data analysis, and scalability at the center of our architecture. We are building the bank technology that should exist and the products we ourselves wanted.

Parallel Universe (YC S12) Is Hiring a Developer Evangelist
text:
Parallel Universe is building next generation server-side open source infrastructure software, which lets developers write simple code that is extremely performant and scalable. We believe while hardware architecture changed drastically almost a decade ago, software hasn't caught up. Current software clashes with hardware, and requires more effort to be expended on scaling rather than on business logic. The problem is most severe in server-side software that ingests real-time data, and needs to respond to a very large number of concurrent requests at low latencies. It facilitates software that is harmonious with modern hardware -- with multi-core and multi-cache, with the storage hierarchy and the IO-to-processing ratio -- rather than software that fights the hardware at every turn. The result is applications that require far less hardware, while at the same time provide much greater performance and headroom for growth.

As a developer evangelist, your job would be to help drive adoption of the Parallel Universe stack. The job is a mix of marketing, coding, sales, and geeking out. On the job you will:

title: Lever – Redefine web apps as realtime distributed systems
text:
https://jobs.lever.co/lever

Lever started in YC S12. Today we've announced our $10M Series A https://blog.lever.co/the-next-chapter/ and shared why collaborative hiring software is the most important web app we can build to improve the world.

We have another vision at Lever: We are redefining what a web app is, and we are building a web app better than any you have used yet -- even if you are already a Lever user. :-)

I worked at Google on the Search team when Google released Chrome and when Wave stunned the world with a futuristic vision. Sarah, our CEO, was part of the small team that spearheaded Google Chrome's initial growth internationally.

We love the Web with an irrational exuberance. URLs have changed the world, and being able to use software that does everything we need simply by visiting one is an incredible experience. Realtime collaboration is a fundamentally transformative idea that has made Google Docs and tools like it 10x better than installed software even with many fewer features.

But why do we sometimes still yearn for the days of installed native software? Native software feels so good. Local software is more responsive, you don't wait to load data after every click, it is always there whether or not the Internet is working. The connectedness of web software is transformative, but we are giving up the great user experience of local editing.

The solution is web apps that are local editors. At Lever, we are writing all of our apps in DerbyJS (http://derbyjs.com/), a new way of thinking about how apps can be written. We use Operational Transformation (OT) and ShareJS (http://sharejs.org/) to edit all data. Users can make edits in realtime or offline and data will be synced automatically. Because OT resolves conflicts, the UI can always be updated immediately.

Browsers already have all of the features we need to store all of the data for an entire application locally in IndexedDB, to make sites available offline with Application Cache, and to provide two way realtime communication with WebSockets. Why aren't applications written this way already? It is just too difficult. Why didn't everyone start using AJAX until jQuery made it trivial? DerbyJS is making the most innovative web application architecture accessible.

If you are an experienced distributed systems engineer up to the challenge of creating the best user experience ever seen in a web app, join us:

title: Deep learning and Speech recognition at Wit.ai
text:
We are building the AI platform that helps thousands of developers create apps and device that understand human language (speech and free text): https://wit.ai

That’s an ambitious goal. Even Google and Apple haven’t completely cracked the problem.

Our approach is different:

- We provide the mass of developers with a simple way to build apps that understand voice commands, and learn from every interaction ; and

- We leverage the community: what Wit.ai learns is shared across developers.

We are a team of nine engineers based in Palo Alto and San Francisco. We were part of Y Combinator W14 and funded by the best VCs.

We’d like to hear from you if:

- You have worked with ASR and/or neural nets "on the field"

- You see yourself as a full-stack software engineer: you like to resolve a problem entirely from hardcore algorithms to implementation.

- You are curious: you can’t resist the urge to solve hard problems, learn new domains, try new things, and you don’t take “that’s impossible” for an answer

- You have done many mistakes (we know you won’t make them again)

- You are ready to learn/do whatever it takes to succeed, from Clojure to Javascript to supporting users to debugging C libraries to assembling furniture.

Some examples of what we’re working on now:

- Leverage C/C++ open source speech to text engines (Kaldi, Sphinx)

- Improve the learning efficiency and the accuracy of our Clojure-based NLP layer

- Build embedded runtimes in Rust/C/C++

- Build iOS and Android SDKs handling low-power magic word (“OK Google”) detection and audio streaming to the API

We are early-stage enough to be able to offer significant equity. We also offer a competitive salary, full benefits, help to relocate to the Bay Area if you need to, and all the perks you expect (we’re probably not the right company if this is your criteria number one though).

If you think you are a good fit, please contact us at jobs at wit.ai with any relevant information that would help us get to know you better (resume, Github, projects, code samples).

title: Kamcord (YC S12) Is Looking for iOS App and SDK Engineers
text:
Kamcord has raised over $10M in seed + Series A funding and is growing like crazy! We’re building a social network centered around gameplay videos for the world’s 1 billion mobile gamers. Growing the community in our iOS app is at the crux of our company’s vision.

We are only a few months into our iOS app development and have tons of both foundational and crazy ideas to work on. We’re built on a really solid foundation though:

BONUS POINTS

Shipped quality apps to the iOS App Store. Solid working knowledge of testing frameworks and build systems for iOS apps. Experience designing robust client-server APIs. You want to dominate at everything from company ping-pong battles to board game nights.

WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN US

We’ve kept our hiring bar really high - you will work with the best. Our app engineering team is just 3 engineers - you’ll get the opportunity to take on a lot of responsibility and grow a ton! title: Want a K-12 teacher to thank you for coding? Come work at Clever (YC S12)
text:
Steve Jobs described education as one of the final frontiers still untouched by modern technology. Clever (YC S12 - https://clever.com) is building the data platform needed for great software to make its way into the classroom. Just like Stripe has made it simple for developers to build payment processing into their apps, Clever has made it easy for developers to build applications for schools using student data.

We're a small, highly technical team with deep experience in education. In under two years, 1 in 6 schools in America has begun using our APIs, meaning that Clever moves data for eight million students every day.

Our newest project is essentially Facebook Connect for education: one identity to tie together all of a student’s learning applications into a cohesive experience. We’re making that happen with our Instant Login service, which allows students to log in once and immediately get access to all their apps: https://www.edsurge.com/n/2014-05-14-no-more-passwords-cleve...

And while we have all the startup perks (a beautiful loft office in SoMa, free lunch, unlimited Amazon credits for learning..) – hands down the best part of the job are the calls and emails from schools describing how much Clever helps them.

As an education company, we’re all about learning personally too – it’s practically a prerequisite to work here. In the past few weeks we’ve done tech talks on things like exoplanets, set theory, and kitesurfing. (We also love a good round of bughouse chess – just ask Magnus Carlsen http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo)

We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

title: How often does a teacher thank you for coding? Come work at Clever to find out!
text:
Steve Jobs described education as one of the final frontiers still untouched by modern technology. Clever (YC S12 - https://clever.com) is building the data platform needed for great software to make its way into the classroom. Just like Stripe has made it simple for developers to build payment processing into their apps, Clever has made it easy for developers to build applications for schools using student data.

We're a small, highly technical team with deep experience in education. In under two years, 1 in 6 schools in America has begun using our APIs, meaning that Clever moves data for eight million students every day.

Our newest project is essentially Facebook Connect for education: one identity to tie together all of a student’s learning applications into a cohesive experience. We’re making that happen with our Instant Login service, which allows students to log in once and immediately get access to all their apps: https://www.edsurge.com/n/2014-05-14-no-more-passwords-clever-shows-off-instant-login

And while we have all the startup perks (a beautiful loft office in SoMa, free lunch, unlimited Amazon credits for learning..) – hands down the best part of the job are the calls and emails from schools describing how much Clever helps them.

As an education company, we’re all about learning personally too – it’s practically a prerequisite to work here. In the past few weeks we’ve done tech talks on things like exoplanets, set theory, and kitesurfing. (We also love a good round of bughouse chess – just ask Magnus Carlsen http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo)

We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

Parallel Universe (YC S12) Is Hiring a Developer Evangelist
text:
Parallel Universe is building next generation server-side open source infrastructure software, that lets developers write simple code that is extremely performant and scalable. We believe while hardware architecture changed drastically almost a decade ago, software hasn't caught up. Current software clashes with hardware, and requires more effort to be expended on scaling rather than on business logic. The problem is most severe in server-side software that ingests real-time data, and needs to respond to a very large number of concurrent requests at low latencies. It facilitates software that is harmonious with modern hardware -- with multi-core and multi-cache, with the storage hierarchy and the IO-to-processing ratio -- rather than software that fights the hardware at every turn. The result is applications that require far less hardware, while at the same time provide much greater performance and headroom for growth.

As a developer evangelist, your job would be to help drive adoption of the Parallel Universe stack. The job is a mix of marketing, coding, sales, and geeking out. On the job you will:

* Write demos and benchmarks, and blog about them

* Write introductory blog posts and tutorials

* Speak at (and organize) developer events and hosted tech-talks

* Study the problems facing potential users, and help direct our software to best address those problems

* Provide support and guidance on technical forums and social media

* Provide on-site support and guidance for customers

* Build and cultivate relationships with US companies

Requirements:

* Experience writing software for the JVM, especially in Java (knowing Clojure is a plus)

* Strong familiarity with modern server-side architectures

* Participation in developer communities

* Strong technical writing skills

* Public speaking experience

* Strong social skills and an outgoing personality

* Residence in the San Francisco Bay Area

You will work from home, but travel in the Bay Area (and occasionally in the rest of the US) to visit companies and participate in events. We offer a competitive salary (with benefits) and equity.

To apply, email jobs@paralleluniverse.co

Parallel Universe Is Looking for a Developer Evangelist in the Bay Area
text:
Parallel Universe is building next generation server-side open source infrastructure software, that lets developers write simple code that is extremely performant and scalable. We believe while hardware architecture changed drastically almost a decade ago, software hasn't caught up. Current software clashes with hardware, and requires more effort to be expended on scaling rather than on business logic. The problem is most severe in server-side software that ingests real-time data, and needs to respond to a very large number of concurrent requests at low latencies. It facilitates software that is harmonious with modern hardware -- with multi-core and multi-cache, with the storage hierarchy and the IO-to-processing ratio -- rather than software that fights the hardware at every turn. The result is applications that require far less hardware, while at the same time provide much greater performance and headroom for growth. As a developer evangelist, your job would be to help drive adoption of the Parallel Universe stack. The job is a mix of marketing, coding, sales, and geeking out. On the job you will: * Write demos and benchmarks, and blog about them

* Write introductory blog posts and tutorials

* Speak at (and organize) developer events and hosted tech-talks

* Study the problems facing potential users, and help direct our software to best address those problems

* Provide support and guidance on technical forums and social media

* Provide on-site support and guidance for customers

* Build and cultivate relationships with US companies

Requirements:

* Experience writing software for the JVM, especially in Java (knowing Clojure is a plus)

* Strong familiarity with modern server-side architectures

* Participation in developer communities

* Strong technical writing skills

* Public speaking experience

* Strong social skills and an outgoing personality

* Residence in the San Francisco Bay Area

You will work from home, but travel in the Bay Area (and occasionally in the rest of the US) to visit companies and participate in events. We offer a competitive salary (with benefits) and equity.

To apply, email jobs@paralleluniverse.co

title: Standard Treasury (YC S13) is working to bring banking to developers
text:
We started Standard Treasury because we were surprised at how difficult it was to build technology in the banking, finance, and payments spaces. This difficulty is because of old legacy technologies, interfaces, and designs at the banks that developers have to work with to build those types of companies.

We found that surprising. The world has moved to more modern web services and APIs, but when working with banks developers have to deal with flat files over FTP (or much much worse), bad documentation, no SDKs, tons of exceptions, funky procedures, etc.

Because of this technological gap things that should be done -- like building mobile apps for the underbanked -- just aren't possible or cost effective. Many of our fellow YC companies come to us over and over again surprised at just how hard it is to do what they want with their banks.

Standard Treasury is fixing that and building a world where tons of developers can build apps on the services that banks and other financial intermediaries provide. It might be infrastructure -- and complicated infrastructure at that -- but we believe that we are building platforms that can meaningfully impact how the world does its banking, and by extension its commerce and trade.

For a variety of reasons, we aren't a bank ourselves, but we build white-labeled developer platforms, developer tools, and more for a variety of banks. We have tons of fun problems to solve -- security and authorization and entitlements, deploying to multiple environments, testing for those environments before deployment, designing platforms for a wide range of developers, designing app stores, online banking, and more for other bank customers, etc.

If any of that sounds interesting to you, shoot me a note at zac@standardtreasury.com

Parallel Universe is Looking for a Developer Evangelist in the Bay Area
text:
Parallel Universe is building next generation server-side open source infrastructure software, that lets developers write simple code that is extremely performant and scalable. We believe while hardware architecture changed drastically almost a decade ago, software hasn't caught up. Current software clashes with hardware, and requires more effort to be expended on scaling rather than on business logic. The problem is most severe in server-side software that ingests real-time data, and needs to respond to a very large number of concurrent requests at low latencies. It facilitates software that is harmonious with modern hardware -- with multi-core and multi-cache, with the storage hierarchy and the IO-to-processing ratio -- rather than software that fights the hardware at every turn. The result is applications that require far less hardware, while at the same time provide much greater performance and headroom for growth. As a developer evangelist, your job would be to help drive adoption of the Parallel Universe stack. The job is a mix of marketing, coding, sales, and geeking out. On the job you will:

* Write demos and benchmarks, and blog about them

* Write introductory blog posts and tutorials

* Speak at (and organize) developer events and hosted tech-talks

* Study the problems facing potential users, and help direct our software to best address those problems

* Provide support and guidance on technical forums and social media

* Provide on-site support and guidance for customers

* Build and cultivate relationships with US companies

Requirements:

* Experience writing software for the JVM, especially in Java (knowing Clojure is a plus)

* Strong familiarity with modern server-side architectures

* Participation in developer communities

* Strong technical writing skills

* Public speaking experience

* Strong social skills and an outgoing personality

* Residence in the San Francisco Bay Area

You will work from home, but travel in the Bay Area (and occasionally in the rest of the US) to visit companies and participate in events. We offer a competitive salary (with benefits) and equity.

To apply, email jobs@paralleluniverse.co

Parallel Universe is Looking for a Developer Evangelist in the Bay Area
text:
Parallel Universe is building next generation server-side open source infrastructure software, that lets developers write simple code that is extremely performant and scalable. We believe while hardware architecture changed drastically almost a decade ago, software hasn't caught up. Current software clashes with hardware, and requires more effort to be expended on scaling rather than on business logic. The problem is most severe in server-side software that ingests real-time data, and needs to respond to a very large number of concurrent requests at low latencies. It facilitates software that is harmonious with modern hardware -- with multi-core and multi-cache, with the storage hierarchy and the IO-to-processing ratio -- rather than software that fights the hardware at every turn. The result is applications that require far less hardware, while at the same time provide much greater performance and headroom for growth.

As a developer evangelist, your job would be to help drive adoption of the Parallel Universe stack. The job is a mix of marketing, coding, sales, and geeking out. On the job you will:

* Write demos and benchmarks, and blog about them

* Write introductory blog posts and tutorials

* Strong technical writing skills

* Public speaking experience

* Strong social skills and an outgoing personality

* Residence in the San Francisco Bay Area

You will work from home, but travel in the Bay Area (and occasionally in the rest of the US) to visit companies and participate in events. We offer a competitive salary (with benefits) and equity.

Mixpanel is looking for a lead operations engineer
text:
Hey HN -

Our engineering team of 12 is currently handling 50K requests per second, 500+ servers, and over 20 billion data points per month.

We're looking for someone to come in and take over the ops load - and hopefully eventually lead a team of operations engineers.

Many of our biggest problems are around infrastructure and scale, and there aren't a lot of startups where you get to work on this stuff.

If you're interested, please drop us a line - jobs@mixpanel.com.

-----

Operations Engineers at Mixpanel are primarily focused on reliability, automation, and physical infrastructure.

In this role you will:

  * Diagnose and fix problems with physical hardware and/or software
  * Automate tasks such as server configuration and deployment
  * Build and maintain monitoring and alerting infrastructure
Our engineering culture:

  * We do very thorough, line-by-line code reviews using GitHub pull requests. This keeps our code quality high and helps us learn.
  * We try to have two people work together on every project (collaborating, not pairing). It's more fun and it results in better code.
  * We practice rapid iteration. If it's better than live, we ship. We also build things so they can go live (whitelisted) long before launch day.
  * We write tests for things that are mission-critical, prone to failure, or cause paranoia. Think billing and datastore code, not Django views.
  * We care about learning. Right now we're reading through Advanced Programming in the Unix Environment.
  * We currently have 9 vim users, 2 IntelliJ, and 1 emacs holdout.
What we are looking for:

  * At least 5 years experience as an Operations Engineer or equivalent
  * Experience running 100+ servers (preferably physical rather than virtual) either as the sole Operations Engineer or as a technical leader in a team. You should be the person that people ask for help when they can't solve an operations problem.
  * Fluency in python or the ability to learn it quickly. You should be comfortable writing code daily.  
  * Strong problem solving ability. You should be able to start with a symptom and methodically work through the problem until you find a root cause.
  * Solid understanding of TCP/IP networking. You should know how and when to use tools like tcpdump, netstat, ethtool, etc.
  * Extensive experience with Linux, especially debugging and performance analysis.
  * US work authorization
Why join Mixpanel?

  * We are profitable, with millions in monthly revenue and over 2,200 paying customers.
  * Mixpanel is still a small company, but we are poised for great growth.
  * Our product is used by companies like amazon.com, Dropbox, Intuit, OpenTable, and Salesforce.
  * We've raised money from top-tier investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia, and Y Combinator.
  * There are a lot of cool people here. You will like the people you work with.
Want to join?

What's the hardest operations problem you've ever diagnosed and solved? Explain it in your cover letter in as much detail as you would like.

Mixpanel is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer supporting workforce diversity.

Build the infrastructure that will power education in the 21st century at Clever
text:
Steve Jobs described education as one of the final frontiers still untouched by modern technology. Clever (YC S12 - https://clever.com) is building the data platform needed for great software to make its way into the classroom. Just like Stripe has made it simple for developers to build payment processing into their apps, Clever has made it easy for developers to build applications for schools using student data.

We're a small, highly technical team with deep experience in education. In under two years, 1 in 6 schools in America has begun using our APIs, meaning that Clever moves data for eight million students every day.

Underneath the hood, Clever runs on a highly modular architecture composed of hundreds of microservices and libraries. A growing team of engineers builds these services and deploys them multiple times per day. This presents a number of unique problems that you will work with the team to solve:

-How do you maintain high velocity (dozens of deployments daily) for services that 20% of schools in the U.S. depend on?

-How do you automatically test, release, and deploy these services and libraries?

-How do these services automatically find and communicate with each other?

-What does the workflow look like for your teammates?

-What open source tools can we use to solve these problems?

The Clever team is actively building on and contributing to bleeding-edge tools such as Docker, Packer, Deis, Synapse, Heka, kubernetes, and Drone. We build almost all of our infrastructure as open source software and work actively with the community to improve the state of the art in deployment and monitoring. While experience with these tools is a huge plus, it's more important to understand the challenges we face and identify existing tools that help us solve them.

If you’re interested, share our passion for improving education, and are in (or willing to move to) San Francisco, we’d love to hear from you.

https://clever.com/about/jobs#distributed-systems-engineer

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

Clever (YC S12) is hiring full-stack engineers to hack education
text:
Steve Jobs described education as one of the final frontiers still untouched by modern technology. Clever (YC S12 - https://clever.com) is building the data platform needed for great software to make its way into the classroom. Just like Stripe has made it simple for developers to build payment processing into their apps, Clever has made it easy for developers to build applications for schools using student data.

We're a small, highly technical team with deep experience in education. In under two years, 1 in 7 schools in America has begun using our APIs, meaning that Clever moves data for eight million students every day.

Our newest project is essentially Facebook Connect for education: one identity to tie together all of a student’s learning applications into a cohesive experience. We’re making that happen with our Instant Login service, which allows students to log in once and immediately get access to all their apps: https://www.edsurge.com/n/2014-05-14-no-more-passwords-cleve...

And while we have all the startup perks (a beautiful loft office in SoMa, free lunch, unlimited Amazon credits for learning..) – hands down the best part of the job are the calls and emails from schools describing how much Clever helps them.

As an education company, we’re all about learning personally too – it’s practically a prerequisite to work here. In the past few weeks we’ve done tech talks on things like exoplanets, set theory, and kitesurfing. (We also love a good round of bughouse chess – just ask Magnus Carlsen http://screencast.com/t/xD7umWfo)

We’re looking for full-stack engineers who can hack in Node, Go, and Python (or are willing to learn), but more importantly, we’re looking for people who share our passion for improving education. If you’re interested, we’d love to hear from you.

https://clever.com/about/jobs

At Clever, we want to work with the best people - applicants of all backgrounds and beliefs are welcome to come improve education with us. We're committed to making our office a safe and comfortable environment for all employees.

title: Systems Engineer? Join us and take on the Telco Giants
text:
SendHub (YC W12) is looking for Systems Engineers. Join us in building a new kind of phone company and fight against the Telco monopolies.

We're looking for a talented and determined individual with a track record of scaling highly available, geographically distributed, fault tolerant services with 100% availability requirements.

About SendHub: We're building tools to make it fast and easy for businesses to communicate with their customers and employees.

Founded to help educators in under resourced communities, we’re taking on the Telecom giants. Hate your phone carrier? Us too. Telecommunications is a duopoly dominated industry, which has systematically suppressed competition over its 150 year history, in order to keep prices unfairly high. We’re going to change this, starting with business phone service. We have a ~$1M annual run rate and closed a $3M Series A in September 2013.

Our Philosophy: We believe in taking care of our customers and each other, so together we can build wonderful products. We work hard delivering the best to our customers and we wouldn't want it any other way. We're hungry and you need to be too.

We're based in Menlo Park, CA, and while we're flexible on working remotely, you'll need to be around the office and eligible to work in the United States. If you're interested, please drop us a line:

===========================

jobs [at] sendhub [dot] com

===========================

As a systems automation and architecture expert you will accelerate SendHub’s ability to respond to emerging issues and enable the team to make changes at scale. You'll lead initiatives to improve our team's operational efforts and set the gold standard when it comes to participating in the on call rotation.

Requirements: You are proficient in a virtualized Linux environment, and know how best to automate and monitor it. You have experience in deploying and managing sharded and replicated postgres environments. You’re comfortable with at least one scripting language e.g. Ruby, Python or Perl. You have in-depth experience deploying and maintaining monitoring tools (Nagios etc.). You are familiar with deployment tools like Chef, Puppet, or rolled your own. You are comfortable configuring routing, firewalls, VPN and DNS You have proficient communication skills and are comfortable interfacing with third party vendors. You strive for mastery and value feedback from others. You’re hands on, yet understand the importance of enabling others.

UI/UX Designer
text:
We’re an off-the-record YC company building financial services tools. We're already cash-flow positive, and laptops, and office snacks, and etc. and so forth. and general good things. Here's what's awesome: we have non-technical customers paying us for an online tool. Everyday, our clients call and email to say that we're making them happy. And that feels great.

But there's one problem: parts of our product are a little bit ugly and a little bit confusing. We're rapidly adding new features, and we're quickly outpacing our design capabilities. In short, it’s time to hire a UX/UI designer.

Our clients use our product for hours at a time. This is their tool for getting their jobs done. It is their workflow. We want it to beautiful and intuitive. It should be easy for a new client to learn, while at the same time, it should make power users feel like they’re flying through their day.

You must have experience with The Struggle of Application Design. And frankly, you should enjoy this struggle, because it’s hard to get things right, but really rewarding when you do.

What would your first day on the job be like? Well, we’ve got a product live right now that processes several hundred orders per day. You now own the design and you will be responsible for improving it. Changes could be simple, like, ‘make this button blue’ or it could be more elaborate like, ‘add tooltips and a new customer tutorial,’ or maybe you might want to redesign aspects of the site from scratch. Ideally, within a couple weeks, clients should be telling us that they’ve noticed small, nice design improvements.

List of Responsibilities: - Design - Usability and Utility are more important (at the moment) than purely visual appeal. As a team, we frequently meet with our clients to learn how they’re using the product. A good candidate for this role will be able to speak to users and feel out their feelings.

List of Skills: - UI/UX design experience - Responsive design experience (a lot of our clients access our site on their phones) - HTML/CSS is great. At the moment, we’re using a lot of Bootstrap. Pixel perfect designs are not (yet) crucial; usability is paramount.

We’re in San Francisco on a trolley-filled street in Union Square. We’re small (3 in-office employees) and we’re still building a culture. If you have ideas for how to build a blissed-out company, we’re all ears. Thinking of moving to San Francisco, but not yet ready to commit? Talk to us.

Send an email to fintechw14@gmail.com telling us about yourself. Include a resume and a portfolio if possible.

title: Shopular (YC W12) is hiring engineers – iOS, Android, full-stack. Sequoia-backed
Run the 42Floors New York Office
text:
We’re opening up our New York office this summer and we’re looking for the perfect person to run it.

Getting it right is the number one strategic priority in the company. You’ll have all the resources you need in terms of money, hiring budget, and support. Your goal will be to scale it into a 50-person, multi-million dollar revenue sales operation as quickly as humanly possible. You’ll manage your own P&L, and have both hiring and firing authority. If this is the job you’ve been waiting for, we want to hear from you.

Let me tell you a little bit of what we’re looking for.

I basically see two types of people that could fill this job, either of which, or some combination of, could be successful.

One type is someone obsessed with commercial real estate, specifically office leasing. Maybe you’ve been a broker before, your family is in the business or you’ve simply been obsessed with it your entire career. You believe that every tenant deserves incredible service and fair representation. You already know many of the players in the market and are excited to partner with them. Both brokers and landlords see you as a known quantity that they can trust. And perhaps your biggest asset is your team work. You want to mentor and inspire junior people on the team. The result of your hard work will be a company culture of hard working, service-oriented hustlers that love coming into work every day. We’re aware that this may be your first experience in a startup, and we’ll make sure that you have plenty of support to get all of the administrative pieces of setting up and running an office done right.

In contrast, the second type of person might not know anything about commercial real estate, but could also be very successful. You’ve probably held senior positions at several startups and experienced hyper growth first hand. What excites you most is that you get to start with just you, and grow from there. You’re in touch with what tenants want because often those tenants are entrepreneurs, and you know tons of entrepreneurs. You have some interest in commercial real estate, but you are more interested in the opportunity to build something really big and special. And you are a quick enough learner so you’ll do your homework and learn the pieces of commercial real estate that you don’t currently know (just like all of us did). Clearly, priority number one will be recruiting someone from the industry to work with you, and we’ll help you with that.

The way we have it set up in San Francisco is that Chris and Justin work together. Justin was an office leasing broker at Cushman Wakefield, but had always wanted to do a startup. Chris came in as a business operations startup guy having been an early hire at RentJuice which got acquired by Zillow. He had a personal interest in commercial real estate but had never extensively worked in it. The partnership of these two in our San Francisco office has worked marvelously. Now we’re trying to build the same sort of dynamic in New York.

As I mentioned, the New York office is going to grow quickly. We have hundreds of tenants a week right now searching for office space on 42Floors. We have a robust tenant-rep referral program working with all of the top brokerages, and now it needs to be run locally. You’ll need to hire customer service reps, account managers, and business development associates. Within six months time we’d love for every 1 out of every 3 small tenants in New York City to start their search on 42Floors.com and, through your efforts, be connected to an outstanding broker that can help them with their search.

The entire experience should be seamless – the lead qualified, the handoff completed, and the tour scheduled. We want to measure and track every aspect of customer happiness. You should be obsessed with the perfect customer service, just as we are.

If you're interested, contact me directly at jason at 42floors

title: YC W14 Fintech company is hiring Machine Learning experts
text:
We are a YC W14 company founded by a Google software engineer and a Morgan Stanley quant trader.

We are applying machine learning, software engineering and rigorous scientific investigation to revamp the lending and securitization space. This is one of finance’s least sexy areas, but is a multi-trillion dollar market- and it’s where the financial crisis started. Bad technology was a major cause, and even after 5 years, no one has fixed it.

Now we’ve found a novel way for a startup to break into the space. We just raised a multimillion dollar seed round from top tier investors including major VCs, Max Levchin, SV Angel and Two Sigma.

We are a full-stack startup, not just another vendor; we make tools so that we can use them. We’re only 8 months old, but already close to being profitable.

Our problems are very technical: we are creating unique ML algorithms, or implementing versions that have never been used in industry before. We work with (or want to work with) approaches that span everything from traditional models like logistic regression, to SVMs, tree models and boosting, amongst many others.

We are munging data from a variety of sources, and applying advanced feature selection and engineering, as well as dimensionality reduction techniques.

THE JOBS

We are looking for full-time employees who will make foundational contributions as part of our machine learning team, which includes both founders.

Obviously, we are looking for smart, determined, hardworking individuals. But most importantly, we are seeking a self-starter who wants a challenge. There are plenty of opportunities available as junior members of established teams where you can coast. This job is NOT that. As an early-stage employee, your role will evolve quickly. You can take on what interests you, while also focusing on your core strengths.

MACHINE LEARNING RESEARCHER

What you bring to the table:

* You share our ideal of pursuit of knowledge, but disdain the not uncommon backbiting and tenure-focus of a traditional academic department

* We’re not just applying algorithms from existing libraries, we want a machine learning savant who understands our business problems, and builds novel ML algorithms that answer the questions we’re asking.

* Ph.D. level research background or industry equivalent, both devising novel algorithms and applying them to real world data.

* Extreme familiarity with supervised learning algorithms is a must.

* Knowledge of customized loss functions, imbalanced data, feature selection, and statistical decision theory is a plus

* Knowledge of quantitative finance is cool – but in no way a requirement.

What you’ll do:

* The market is our lab. You’ll investigate data, construct a hypothesis, and instead of writing a paper, actually apply your ideas and make money!

* We’re exploring ideas from across computer science and statistics, including supervised learning, natural language processing, imbalanced data and anomaly detection, deep learning, time series, feature extraction and selection, and many, many other areas.

* We are, strangely enough, very interested in ideas from biostatistics, survival analysis and epidemiology, so applied experience (or even interest) in these areas would be cool.

MACHINE LEARNING SOFTWARE ENGINEER

What you bring to the table:

* Professional experience applying machine learning techniques and building production ML systems. You should know your decision trees and SVMs, and be ready to learn a lot more!

* Coding skill in Python, C++ or similar. We currently use Python, but welcome developers of any background, as long as you can pick up Python.

* We value correctness, maintainability, elegance, and testability of code. We want to do things the right way over just getting things ‘done’. We’re strict about our code style and quality so that you don’t have to spend your time tracking down other peoples’ bugs.

* Experience in functional programming languages such as Clojure or OCaml would be a plus.

* Knowledge of quantitative finance is cool – but in no way a requirement.

What you’ll do

* Participate in cutting edge research in artificial intelligence and machine learning applications.

* Develop and implement solutions for real world, large-scale problems.

* We’re exploring ideas from across computer science and statistics, including supervised learning, natural language processing, imbalanced data and anomaly detection, deep learning and time varying systems.

What we offer

* As an early employee, you get to shape the company culture and make foundational contributions to the code base.

* Market rate salary and generous equity package

* Standard Benefits - Medical and dental insurance.

* Flexible hours and open vacation policy

This work is not for everyone, but if you’re interested, and think you might be qualified, email us at yc.fintech@gmail.com to learn more. We are located in San Francisco, CA

title: True Link Financial (YC S13) is hiring a senior Java engineer
text:
We're a San Francisco-based fraud protection startup targeting credit card fraud against seniors as the first step in a much bigger play. In order to do that, we had to figure out how to issue and process Visa cards. That's one of the most difficult things a startup can set themselves up to do, and we did it.

Now we want to bring on someone who can own the heck out of this highly performant, scalable system. Processing card transactions is really hard because you're dealing with esoteric encodings, you have to never miss anything, and you have a fifth of a second or so to respond. That means you're doing clever local read slaves because light can't cross the country in time to load the right stuff out of the database. It also means you're using futures to start database loads and do the processing you can in the meantime, and then timing out and responding if your database response doesn't come in time to act on. It's the kind of thing you implement a first version to figure out what you need, and then rewrite it in go when the codebase stabilizes.

We're looking for a senior Java engineer. You need to be conversant with Java socket-based servers in a high-performance environment. You'll be responsible for the design, enhancement, and implementation of a high-availability set of distributed servers with millisecond-level performance requirements. Extensive experience with designing and implementing security, reliable systems, and monitoring are musts. You should be comfortable getting down to byte-level in protocols, and know how to test and tune Java applications.

The technology is complex and this role has substantial ownership of technical strategy and execution associated. We are looking for a very experienced engineer and are offering CTO-level equity. We're early enough that you'll have a meaningful equity stake and, at the same time, we're well funded, so you won't have to worry that we'll run out of money and fire everyone in a week. Free lunch, Apple products, and a kick-ass team are also part of the package.

Must-haves:

* You have 5+ years of programming experience in Java

* You're familiar with and comfortable in Java 1.7 and up

* You're comfortable working with SQL databases

Pluses:

* You're familiar with software development for financial services

* You have experience in financial services

* You have experience with ISO 8583 messages

* You have distributed systems experience

Send resumes and inquiries to jobs@truelinkfinancial.com
