title: We’re hiring for sales and ops at 42Floors
text:
You may be thinking…

Wait! What are you guys doing?! All job posts on Hacker News are supposed to be for hackers.

And you’re kinda right. I know the audience here are hackers. But hackers have friends that are interested in startups. And I bet at least a few of you get asked which startup your job-hunting friend should apply to. And at 42Floors, we like for every person on the team to be from the startup community. So, actually, the single best way for a candidate to get an account management job offer is from a referral from a hacker.

…So consider this one of those posts that you should forward on if you feel it warrants it.

So, since I need to make this compelling enough for you to forward to your smartest, self-motivated, awesome friend, here’s a little about 42Floors and what type of experience one would have as an entry level account manager:

42Floors makes it easy to search for commercial real estate online. We’re like Zillow for office space. We’re a team of 25 and we’ve raised 17M from NEA, Thrive, Bessemer, YC and many others.

Our site is blowing up right now with massive demand that we simply can’t keep up with. We’re hiring as many account management specialists and sales people as we can. Over the next year, we need to reach out to virtually every landlord and broker in the U.S. We’re going to build a really big team of people to do it, but right now the account management team has just 5 people on it.

It’s going to be an incredible experience for whoever joins the team right now. Not in 3 months, not in 6 months, but right now when all the fun company building parts are still to be had.

Startups are usually run totally flat and our’s is an extreme example of that. There will definitely be people to support the account management team, but the best employees are those that are not only capable of figuring things out, but prefer it that way.

It doesn’t matter whether a candidate knows about commercial real estate or not. We’ll teach that part. And it doesn’t matter whether they have experience in sales or account management. We can help with that part as well. But they need to love all things startups. They need to be super motivated.

And if you know someone that are those things, tell them to apply to http://42floors.com/jobs.

text:
Hi HN,

I'm looking for excellent systems engineers to join the team at Mixpanel. We’re a 50 person team (11 eng) in San Francisco, and we’ve built the most flexible analytics platform in the world.

The Systems team (currently 3) is primarily focused on low-level systems programming, scaling, and infrastructure.

Responsibilities of this role include:

  * Working on our custom datastore (written from the ground up in C)
  * Scaling the data processing pipeline (currently handling > 50K requests per second)
  * Building notification delivery infrastructure (currently sending > 100M emails & push notifications per month)
  * General improvements to performance, reliability, and security
If I was looking for a job, the first question I’d ask is “what is your engineering culture like?”. So here’s what we care about:

  * We do very thorough, line-by-line code reviews using GitHub pull requests. This keeps our code quality high and helps us learn.
  * We try to have two people work together on every project (collaborating, not pairing). It's more fun and it results in better code.
  * We practice rapid iteration. If it's better than live, we ship. We also build things so they can go live (whitelisted) long before launch day.
  * We write tests for things that are mission-critical, prone to failure, or cause paranoia. Think billing and datastore code, not Django views.
  * We care about learning. Right now we're reading through Advanced Programming in the Unix Environment.
  * We currently have 8 vim users, 2 IntelliJ, and 1 emacs holdout.
We’re looking for candidates with:

  * at least 3 years of experience in industry
  * mastery of at least one programming language
  * US work authorization
  * passion - you have built (and are dying to show us) something you're proud of, outside of work/school
  * strong problem solving ability
  * attention to detail
  * you code as fluently as you speak
Why join Mixpanel?

  * We are profitable, with millions in monthly revenue and over 2,200 paying customers.
  * Mixpanel is still a small company, but we are poised for great growth.
  * Our product is used by companies like amazon.com, Dropbox, Intuit, OpenTable, and Salesforce.
  * We've raised money from top-tier investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia, and Y Combinator.
  * There are a lot of cool people here. You will like the people you work with.
If this sounds interesting, please get in touch. I’d love to hear about the systems you’ve built & scaling problems you’ve solved.

Tim Trefren tim@mixpanel.com

For more info, check out http://mixpanel.com/jobs

We’re hiring account managers at 42Floors
text:
You may be thinking…

Wait! What are you guys doing?! All job posts on Hacker News are supposed to be for hackers.

And you’re kinda right. I know the audience here are hackers. But hackers have friends that are interested in startups. And I bet at least a few of you get asked which startup your job-hunting friend should apply to. And at 42Floors, we like for every person on the team to be from the startup community. So, actually, the single best way for a candidate to get an account management job offer is from a referral from a hacker. (By the way, we offer $1000 for referrals...)

…So consider this one of those posts that you should forward on if you feel it warrants it.

So, since I need to make this compelling enough for you to forward to your smartest, self-motivated, awesome friend, here’s a little about 42Floors and what type of experience one would have as an entry level account manager:

42Floors makes it easy to search for commercial real estate online. We’re like Zillow for office space. We’ve a team of 16 and we’ve raised 17M from NEA, Thrive, Bessemer, YC and many others.

Our site is blowing up right now with massive demand that we simply can’t keep up with. We’re hiring as many account management specialists and sales people as we can – all entry level positions. Over the next year, we need to reach out to virtually every landlord and broker in the U.S. We’re going to build a really big team of people to do it, but right now the account management team has just 5 people on it.

It’s going to be an incredible experience for whoever joins the team right now. Not in 3 months, not in 6 months, but right now when all the fun company building parts are still to be had.

Startups are usually run totally flat and ours is an extreme example of that. There will definitely be people to support the account management team, but the best employees are those that are not only capable of figuring things out, but prefer it that way.

It doesn’t matter whether a candidate knows about commercial real estate or not. We’ll teach that part. And it doesn’t matter whether they have experience in sales or account management. We can help with that part as well. But they need to love all things startups. They need to be super motivated.

And if you know someone that are those things, tell them to apply to http://42floors.com/jobs.

Have them mention your referral and we’ll send you $1000!

title: Wit.AI (YC W14) is hiring full-stack engineers in Palo Alto
text:
We are building the AI platform that helps 3000+ developers create apps that understand human language.

That’s an ambitious goal. After years of research and billions of dollars invested, even Google and Apple haven’t completely cracked the problem.

Our approach is different:

- We provide the mass of developers with a simple way to build apps that understand voice commands, and learn from every interaction ; and

- We leverage the community: what Wit.AI learns is shared across developers.

We are a team of four engineers based in Palo Alto. We were part of Y Combinator W14 and funded by investors like Andreessen Horowitz, NEA and Ignition.

We’d like to hear from you if:

- You are a full-stack software engineer: you know how to build entire projects/features from Web UI to core ML algorithms

- You are curious: you can’t resist the urge to solve hard problems, learn new domains, try new things, and you don’t take “that’s impossible” for an answer

- You have done many mistakes (we know you won’t make them again)

text:
Calling all community managers who love startups, cooking, and learning about food!

Like our name might have given away, Gobble (http://gobble.com) is a startup in the food space. We work with top local chefs to bring the world’s favorite dishes freshly-made to your door. Our dishes are inspired by the individuality, creativity and cultural heritage of our chefs from around the globe. From Dragon Rolls to Braised Brisket, there's a mouthwatering dish for everyone. Our operations are up and running, and it's time to go beyond doing the bare minimum. We need a smart, energetic team player to join our team as the first ever Gobble Community Manager.

We know this title usually suggests some kind of social media management, but this role goes way beyond that. When we say community manager, we mean that you will be the person who represents who we are to the outside world. You will also be responsible for bringing outside input to our team to help us continually improve our product. We want someone who can sit at the team meetings with us as an equal with the founders and really think about what we want to communicate to customers and how we can do better.

Here's the starter list of duties:

- Customer happiness. you will be talking directly with customers every day and making sure they're happy with our product. If they're not, you'll also be the one to help us fix that. You will be the frontline of defense when it comes to making sure we are attending to customers' needs.

- Writing our weekly newsletter. this is our one source of outgoing communication so it's pretty important to make sure it conveys exciting product updates and food world content that aligns spot on with our company values.

- Incorporating customer feedback into the product. You'll be the one hearing all their feedback and making sure we can turn it into actionable product changes.

- Whatever occurs to you and whatever comes your way. You are joining an early early stage startup so we expect you to figure out what needs to get done so that we can successfully communicate with our clients and implement it as needed. We also expect you to be flexible and take on any necessary tasks that might not fit your job description.

Here are the qualifications for the position:

- A bachelor's degree. If you don't have one, feel free to convince us of why you're still a fit.

- Team spirit. Have we mentioned we're a tight-knit group? We want someone who wants to be part of a team and is a good team played and contributor.

- Willingness to dive in. We're not looking for someone who wants a 9-5 job. This is just not what that is! We want someone who will join us and think and act like a company founder.

- Precision. We're a team that doesn't miss a detail or a beat. You should be highly organized and 100% on your game at all times.

- Previous experience in a writing role. Whether it's newsletters, emails, blog posts, or your college newspaper, you can quickly create content for our customers that is both creative and clear.

- Previous experience in a people-facing role. Maybe you worked at an ice cream store one summer, or you worked in communications at a non-profit, or you made sales calls for a past startup. Grace under pressure is the key to success here.

- Excitement to join an early-stage company. Early-stage companies are a world of their own. They're small and hectic, and it takes someone who loves this environment to succeed in it.

- Experience working at a startup is preferred, but not required. It would be helpful if you've been in this environment before and know what it's about.

How to apply:

This competitive role carries significant potential for growth within the company. We are a down to earth team with outworldly food perks. If you are interested in this high-learning and high-impact opportunity, please send your resume and a note of interest to Justin at hiring@gobble.com.

Stealth YC W14 FinTech company is hiring Machine Learning experts
text:
We are a YC W14 company founded by a Google software engineer and a Morgan Stanley quant trader.

We are applying machine learning, software engineering and rigorous scientific investigation to revamp the lending and securitization space. This is one of finance’s least sexy areas, but is a multi-trillion dollar market- and it’s where the financial crisis started. Bad technology was a major cause, and even after 5 years, no one has fixed it.

Now we’ve found a novel way for a startup to break into the space. We just raised a multimillion dollar seed round from top tier investors including major VCs, Max Levchin, SV Angel and Two Sigma.

We are a full-stack startup, not just another vendor; we make tools so that we can use them. We’re only 8 months old, but already close to being profitable.

Our problems are very technical: we are creating unique ML algorithms, or implementing versions that have never been used in industry before. We work with (or want to work with) approaches that span everything from traditional models like logistic regression, to SVMs, tree models and boosting, amongst many others.

We are munging data from a variety of sources, and applying advanced feature selection and engineering, as well as dimensionality reduction techniques.

THE JOBS

We are looking for full-time employees who will make foundational contributions as part of our machine learning team, which includes both founders.

Obviously, we are looking for smart, determined, hardworking individuals. But most importantly, we are seeking a self-starter who wants a challenge. There are plenty of opportunities available as junior members of established teams where you can coast. This job is NOT that. As an early-stage employee, your role will evolve quickly. You can take on what interests you, while also focusing on your core strengths.

MACHINE LEARNING RESEARCHER

What you bring to the table:

* You share our ideal of pursuit of knowledge, but disdain the not uncommon backbiting and tenure-focus of a traditional academic department

* We’re not just applying algorithms from existing libraries, we want a machine learning savant who understands our business problems, and builds novel ML algorithms that answer the questions we’re asking.

* Ph.D. level research background or industry equivalent, both devising novel algorithms and applying them to real world data.

* Extreme familiarity with supervised learning algorithms is a must.

* Knowledge of customized loss functions, imbalanced data, feature selection, and statistical decision theory is a plus

* Knowledge of quantitative finance is cool – but in no way a requirement.

What you’ll do:

* The market is our lab. You’ll investigate data, construct a hypothesis, and instead of writing a paper, actually apply your ideas and make money!

* We’re exploring ideas from across computer science and statistics, including supervised learning, natural language processing, imbalanced data and anomaly detection, deep learning, time series, feature extraction and selection, and many, many other areas.

* We are, strangely enough, very interested in ideas from biostatistics, survival analysis and epidemiology, so applied experience (or even interest) in these areas would be cool.

MACHINE LEARNING SOFTWARE ENGINEER

What you bring to the table:

* Professional experience applying machine learning techniques and building production ML systems. You should know your decision trees and SVMs, and be ready to learn a lot more!

* Coding skill in Python, C++ or similar. We currently use Python, but welcome developers of any background, as long as you can pick up Python.

* We value correctness, maintainability, elegance, and testability of code. We want to do things the right way over just getting things ‘done’. We’re strict about our code style and quality so that you don’t have to spend your time tracking down other peoples’ bugs.

* Experience in functional programming languages such as Clojure or OCaml would be a plus.

* Knowledge of quantitative finance is cool – but in no way a requirement.

What you’ll do

* Participate in cutting edge research in artificial intelligence and machine learning applications.

* Develop and implement solutions for real world, large-scale problems.

* We’re exploring ideas from across computer science and statistics, including supervised learning, natural language processing, imbalanced data and anomaly detection, deep learning and time varying systems.

What we offer

* As an early employee, you get to shape the company culture and make foundational contributions to the code base.

* Market rate salary and generous equity package

* Standard Benefits - Medical and dental insurance.

* Flexible hours and open vacation policy

This work is not for everyone, but if you’re interested, and think you might be qualified, email us at yc.fintech@gmail.com to learn more.

We're located in San Francisco, CA.

We are seeking a Sr. Developer who has a genuine interest in data security. As our first engineering hire, you will play a critical role in the growth of TrueVault. Our ideal candidate has 3 - 5 years of experience working at a security-focused company (e.g., Stripe, Braintree, Cloudflare, etc.). This is not a file-sharing and collaboration tool; TrueVault is a broader platform for all healthcare applications and services. Our customers are developers working on mobile apps, wearable devices and anything healthcare related. Healthcare is our beachhead. We envision TrueVault as the default database store for all secure data.

What you need to know: TrueVault is a Python shop but we welcome developers with any background (as long as you are willing to pick up Python quickly). But much more important than the languages you know, you must have worked on a product or at a company where data security is the primary concern.

So when we review a resume, we place a lot of emphasis on extracurricular activities like hobby projects, Stackoverflow / GitHub contributions, and other things that show us you are all about technology. Now that you know what we are looking for, apply at your own risk :)

title: Join Firebase as a Senior Database Engineer
text:
Do you want to make the process of building, deploying, and operating modern cloud applications radically easier? Join us and change the way software is built. We (Firebase — YC S11) are hiring a senior database engineer in SF.

At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only between servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier. Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

Over 500,000 devices are connected to Firebase's servers at any given time, and 10s of millions of users use a Firebase-powered app every day.

Our team is serious about computer science as a discipline -- we have folks hailing from Mozilla, Google, Microsoft, Twitter, HP, Adobe, Akamai, and Adroll -- but WE NEED YOU to take Firebase to the next level. We tackle some of the hardest problems in computer science every day: large distributed systems, data merging and conflict resolution, data security, language design, high performance networking, index generation, etc.

If you've previously worked on the internals of databases and you're looking for your next challenge, please drop us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

title: Join Firebase as Production Engineer #2
text:
Do you want to make the process of building, deploying, and operating modern cloud applications radically easier? Join us and change the way software is built.

At Firebase, we're building the first realtime database-as-a-service. Every other database was designed to be downloaded and run on a business's own servers behind a firewall. Firebase is different -- it's a cloud service that's managed directly by the people who make it. By centralizing operations in the hands of our team, we can provide a superior experience for our developers, increased reliability, and massive efficiencies of scale. Our small team already manages the data for 10s of thousands of developers.

If you join Firebase, you will be the second engineer on a brand new team. You’ll be responsible for ensuring that Firebase is a trusted solution for mission-critical realtime applications. Your mandate will be to design and build any systems needed to make Firebase reliable, scalable, secure, and fault-tolerant. You’ll have the freedom to design everything — software, hardware, networks — from the ground up to serve high performance, realtime applications that are based on persistent network connections (ie. websockets, long-polling) and a synchronization paradigm.

As a Production Engineer, you’ll be tasked with: (1) Architecting our networking and storage systems (2) Ensuring the security of the Firebase service and all of our infrastructure (3) Building monitoring, backup, and load testing tools (4) Managing our automated build, CI, and deployment systems (5) Provisioning new hardware and services (6) Handling alerts as part of our 24x7 on-call rotation (7) Advising the rest of the engineering team on best practices regarding security, reliability, and scaling

We need some smart, creative, and disciplined engineers to take Firebase to the next level. The ideal candidate would have: (1) a keen attention to detail (2) strong programming skills (3) a solid working knowledge of Linux and networking (4) a healthy paranoia for security concerns (5) a drive to automate things

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to.

Second, we care a lot about cultivating a great work environment. This is our happy place. We're friendly people, we have a light-weight engineering process, and we have a sweet 3 story penthouse office in SoMa.

Third, you can have a big impact here. We're a small team (but growing very quickly), and you'll have a big say in the direction of the company. And, since we're serious about changing the way software is built, you could have a big impact on the way all software is made. We won't stop until the "refresh" button is a thing of the past.

If you're interested, send us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

title: Come hack on analytics at Mixpanel (YC S09)
text:
Hi HN - Tim from Mixpanel here. I'm looking for engineers who are a) smart & competent b) sociable and c) passionate. The eng team is only 10 right now, so there's a lot of room for you to make an impact.

You can reach me directly at tim@mixpanel.com.

---

Mixpanel is the most advanced analytics platform ever for mobile and web. We help companies build better products.

Our engineering team of 10 is handling 40K requests per second, 400+ servers, and over 20 billion data points per month.

The Product Engineering team is composed of full-stack engineers who are responsible for all user-facing parts of Mixpanel: APIs, reporting interfaces, data visualization, and client libraries.

Recent projects include Mobile surveys (iOS, Android, JS, Python, C) and Live view (JS, Python, C, Redis).

Our engineering culture

  * We do very thorough, line-by-line code reviews using GitHub pull requests. This keeps our code quality high and helps us learn.
  * We try to have two people work together on every project (collaborating, not pairing). It's more fun and it results in better code.
  * We practice rapid iteration. If it's better than live, we ship. We also build things so they can go live (whitelisted) long before launch day.
  * We write tests for things that are mission-critical, prone to failure, or cause paranoia. Think billing and datastore code, not Django views.
  * We care about learning. Right now we're reading through Advanced Programming in the Unix Environment.
  * We are 80% vim, 10% emacs, and 10% IntelliJ.
What we are looking for

  * at least 2 years of experience in industry
  * mastery of at least one programming language
  * passion - you have built (and are dying to show us) something you're proud of, outside of work/school
  * strong problem solving ability
  * attention to detail
  * you code as fluently as you speak
Why join Mixpanel?

  * We are profitable, with millions in monthly revenue and over 1,700 paying customers.
  * Mixpanel is still a small company (38), but we are poised for great growth.
  * Our product is used by companies like amazon.com, Dropbox, Intuit, OpenTable, and Salesforce.
  * We've raised money from top-tier investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia, and Y Combinator.
  * There are a lot of cool people here. You will like the people you work with.
Want to join?

What's the hardest thing you have ever built? Explain it in as much detail as you would like. Email jobs@mixpanel.com with your answer and resume.

title: Position a machine learning product. Lead product marketing at Sift Science
text:

You will wear many hats, and will have to think on your feet. Last year there was $4B in online fraud and 70% of that was driven by organized crime. The opponents are no longer script kiddies -- they’re just as smart and capable as any of us, and their attacks are evolving in both scale and sophistication. As the world becomes more connected, this problem will only get worse. We’re building a large-scale machine learning system paired with elegant visualization/UI tools to help e-commerce businesses take a stand. We’re literally fighting bad guys, and have big plans beyond fraud.

Our team includes several ex-Googlers with experience spanning e-commerce analytics, search quality, ads quality, and speech recognition. We value respect, collaboration and creativity, and don't take ourselves too seriously. We want to create a great place to work -- a company is nothing without its people.

* Translate new product/technical capabilities into meaningful customer benefits, including concrete positioning and messaging for all new product features

* Generate and nurture qualified leads via content marketing (whitepapers, case studies, social media, infographics, webinars, etc.) and digital marketing (SEO, A/B testing, email, ads, etc.)

* Evangelize and demonstrate the product to relevant technical and nontechnical audiences at tradeshows and conferences

* Plan and execute successful product launches, working closely with product, engineering, PR, design, support and sales

* Create copy, diagrams, videos and concepts to bring Sift Science to life on the web site, in collateral, and in presentation materials

Our investors include Union Square Ventures, First Round Capital, Max Levchin (PayPal co-founder), Marc Benioff (Salesforce CEO), Chris Dixon (Andreesen Horowitz), Y Combinator, SV Angel, and others well-versed in e-commerce, payments, and enterprise software. We offer market salary, meaningful equity, health insurance, etc. just like everyone else. But what’s most important is the work you do and who you do it with. Let’s make the Internet a better place. Send your resume / GitHub to jobs+hn@siftscience.com

title: Help design the future of banking at Standard Treasury (YC S13)
text:
Job Description

We're seeking a designer who is passionate about creating elegant web interfaces to simplify complicated underlying platforms. You will be responsible for designing and prototyping the frontend and user interface for all aspects of multiple co-branded and white-labeled banking platforms for some of the world’s largest financial institutions. We care deeply about having the best developer experience possible, and our frontend is just as important as the API itself. You will be responsible for incorporating the visual identities and branding guidelines of multiple banks into your designs and mocks for developer portals, API docs, dashboards, management consoles, example apps, marketing materials, and more.

Great candidates should be comfortable incorporating analytics, user research, A/B testing, and their own intuition and creativity to create delightful experiences across all of our partners’ white-label or co-branded platform experiences. You should also be capable of collaborating with people across the spectrum from platform engineers to nontechnical banking partners in designing new features and enhancing the user experience. Being able to build working prototypes of your designs is a big plus.

Requirements

-Empathy with developers. Passion for creating a superlative developer experience down to every last detail.

-Opinionated intuition around usability, with excellent communication skills to explain your decisions.

-Experience leading an iterative design process incorporating partner feedback, user research, A/B testing, and rapid launches to test your hypotheses.

-Always working to improve yourself and constructively support the team around you.

-Bonus: enough frontend engineering experience to build working prototypes of your designs.

-Bonus: experience conducting usability studies.

About Standard Treasury

Standard Treasury helps bank harness the power of developers and developer ecosystems. We are building white-labeled and co-branded RESTful API platforms for commercial banks (e.g., api.[bank].com, developers.[bank].com, and appstore.[bank].com). Our platforms will enable bank customers to automate their financial back offices, as well as for app developers to integrate financial information and products directly into their apps in novel ways never before possible.

Last year, bank technology vendors made over $63 billion a year selling bank software. Most of our competitors were spun out of banks decades ago. We bring the Silicon Valley mindset of creativity, great technology, and willingness to challenge the status quo to this massive industry. A modern, technology-forward, API-driven approach can consume much of the market.

We are a small team based in San Francisco and are looking for the right people to join us. Our team has previously worked at Facebook, Stripe, Disqus, Microsoft, and more. We are fortunate to be backed by Y Combinator, several large venture firms, and many well-known angel investors in our quest to remake financial technology.

Compensation and Perks

You can expect

Great benefits. Medical, vision, and dental insurance for you and your dependents.

Great comp. Salary and equity. We know some people have a greater risk appetite than others and we’re interested in finding the right balance for you.

Great perks. Free breakfast, lunch, and dinner, snacks, a stocked fridge, laundry service, gym membership, Clipper card, and house cleaning.

Great flexibility. Flexible hours, open vacation policy, paid maternity/paternity.

Great tools. Build your ideal workstations so you can have the tools you want and need. Buy the books you need or want on Amazon. Need a Kindle for your commute — get it. The corporate Amex can be used for all expenses under a standard of trust & reasonableness.

Standard Treasury's Values

Excellence. We are building a team of great women and men who work hard, have a passion for perfection, and don’t tolerate bullshit.

Candor. We practice internal transparency and are candid about our finances, business development, and planning processes.

Quality. We build bank software -- our motto is more “slow and steady wins the race” than “move fast and break things”. Our critical technical values are security, reliability, consistency, maintainability, and craftsmanship. We emphasize tremendous attention to detail and build software that lasts.

Collaboration. We use Phabricator and support each other with code reviews. We have a healthy culture of debate without argumentation.

Entrepreneurship. We encourage people to set their own direction. We are looking for senior engineers who can lead product decisions. All engineers are able to suggest, research, and lead architectural changes, contribute to and suggest revisions to our roadmap, and create new coding guidelines and have them be enforced.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

title: The Human Diagnosis Project
text:
Why? It's a question you should ask yourself often. Are you spending your brief moment in the universe focused on what matters most?

We ask ourselves this question every day. We think what matters most is the health of oneself and one's loved ones. Don't believe us? Tell us how much time you spend thinking about anything else next time you or someone you care about is sick.

The best minds of our generation are building companies to peddle mobile ads, share photos, and enable governments to spy on their citizens. The global internet/mobile infrastructure gives us the ability, and the responsibility, to solve many of humankind's most challenging problems.

It's why we're building the Human Diagnosis Project, a single open system that comprehensively maps any human health problem to its possible diagnoses. Join us in building the future of medicine.

---

Due to the scope/nature of the Project, the interview process will be rigorous. If you're interested, please drop us a note at team@humandx.org with one (or more) of the following:

title: Growth/Press Hacker
Firebase (YC S11) is hiring core developers in SF.
text:
At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only between servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier. Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

Over 500,000 devices are connected to Firebase's servers at any given time, and 10s of millions of users use a Firebase-powered app every day.

Our team is serious about computer science as a discipline -- we have folks hailing from Mozilla, Microsoft, Twitter, HP, Adobe, Akamai, Salesforce, and Adroll -- but WE NEED YOU to take Firebase to the next level. We tackle some of the hardest problems in computer science every day: large distributed systems, data merging and conflict resolution, data security, language design, high performance networking, index generation, etc.

If you've previously worked on the internals of databases, spent time optimizing network stacks, or if you feel you're an especially strong algorithms programmer, please drop us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

Sift Science (http://siftscience.com). Lead our marketing initiatives in sunny/foggy San Francisco. You will wear many hats, and will have to think on your feet.

Last year there was $4B in online fraud and 70% of that was driven by organized crime. The opponents are no longer script kiddies -- they’re just as smart and capable as any of us, and their attacks are evolving in both scale and sophistication. As the world becomes more connected, this problem will only get worse. We’re building a large-scale machine learning system paired with elegant visualization/UI tools to help e-commerce businesses take a stand. We’re literally fighting bad guys, and have big plans beyond fraud.

Our team includes several ex-Googlers with experience spanning e-commerce analytics, search quality, ads quality, and speech recognition. We value respect, collaboration and creativity, and don't take ourselves too seriously. We want to create a great place to work -- a company is nothing without its people.

Responsibilities:

* Translate new product/technical capabilities into meaningful customer benefits, including concrete positioning and messaging for all new product features

* Generate and nurture qualified leads via content marketing (whitepapers, case studies, social media, infographics, webinars, etc.) and digital marketing (SEO, A/B testing, email, ads, etc.)

* Evangelize and demonstrate the product to relevant technical and nontechnical audiences at tradeshows and conferences

* Plan and execute successful product launches, working closely with product, engineering, PR, design, support and sales

* Create copy, diagrams, videos and concepts to bring Sift Science to life on the web site, in collateral, and in presentation materials

Our investors include Union Square Ventures, First Round Capital, Max Levchin (PayPal co-founder), Marc Benioff (Salesforce CEO), Chris Dixon (Andreesen Horowitz), Y Combinator, SV Angel, and others well-versed in e-commerce, payments, and enterprise software. We offer market salary, meaningful equity, health insurance, etc. just like everyone else. But what’s most important is the work you do and who you do it with. Everything else is just icing on the cake.

Let’s make the Internet a better place. Send your resume / GitHub to jobs+hn@siftscience.com

title: Bored? Spend your summer building ML algos on top of $250M in transactional data
Help integrate with the world's largest banks at Standard Treasury (YC S13)
text:
Job Description

Build the glue that integrates Standard Treasury’s platforms with some of the world’s largest financial institutions. A passion for reverse-engineering illogical choices and exposing clean interfaces to internal developers is a must. You should love puzzles. We don’t expect that you’re an expert at (or maybe even heard of) IBM WebSphere or Oracle SOA technologies, but you shouldn’t be scared of them, either. The idea of working with a COBOL engineer at a bank, if that’s what it takes, should excite you -- even if it drives you a little crazy.

We expect that you’ve proven yourself patient and versatile in the past. Great candidates will have experience developing software with queuing, caching, concurrent processing, event monitoring, and management.

Requirements

Experience with Python. Experience with Java, Scala, or C# in an enterprise environment a plus.

Knowledge of and experience working with a variety of protocols and formats involved in bank integrations, such as HTTP, SOAP, JSON, XML Schema, WS-, RMI, SAML, OAuth, etc.

The ability to pick up new programming languages and systems very quickly.

Deep love of building elegant, maintainable, and well-documented code. Abstracting and refactoring should be a passion, not a chore.

Drive to learn new things and go above and beyond the call of duty.

Always working to improve yourself and constructively support the team around you.

Bonus: Experience with WebLogic, WebSphere, and other J2EE technologies used by large financial institutions.

Bonus: Experience with security technologies such as X.509 PKI, XML digital signatures, SAML, and OAuth.

About Standard Treasury*

Standard Treasury helps bank harness the power of developers and developer ecosystems. We are building white-labeled and co-branded RESTful API platforms for commercial banks (e.g., api.[bank].com, developers.[bank].com, and appstore.[bank].com). Our platforms will enable bank customers to automate their financial back offices, as well as for app developers to integrate financial information and products directly into their apps in novel ways never before possible.

Last year, bank technology vendors made over $63 billion a year selling bank software. Most of our competitors were spun out of banks decades ago. We bring the Silicon Valley mindset of creativity, great technology, and willingness to challenge the status quo to this massive industry. A modern, technology-forward, API-driven approach can consume much of the market.

We are a small team based in San Francisco and are looking for the right people to join us. Our team has previously worked at Facebook, Stripe, Disqus, Microsoft, and more. We are fortunate to be backed by Y Combinator, several large venture firms, and many well-known angel investors in our quest to remake financial technology.

Compensation and Perks

You can expect

Great benefits. Medical, vision, and dental insurance for you and your dependents.

Great comp. Salary and equity. We know some people have a greater risk appetite than others and we’re interested in finding the right balance for you.

Great perks. Free breakfast, lunch, and dinner, snacks, a stocked fridge, laundry service, gym membership, Clipper card, and house cleaning.

Great flexibility. Flexible hours, open vacation policy, paid maternity/paternity.

Great tools. Build your ideal workstations so you can have the tools you want and need. Buy the books you need or want on Amazon. Need a Kindle for your commute — get it. The corporate Amex can be used for all expenses under a standard of trust & reasonableness.

Standard Treasury's Values

Excellence. We are building a team of great women and men who work hard, have a passion for perfection, and don’t tolerate bullshit.

Candor. We practice internal transparency and are candid about our finances, business development, and planning processes.

Quality. We build bank software -- our motto is more “slow and steady wins the race” than “move fast and break things”. Our critical technical values are security, reliability, consistency, maintainability, and craftsmanship. We emphasize tremendous attention to detail and build software that lasts.

Collaboration. We use Phabricator and support each other with code reviews. We have a healthy culture of debate without argumentation.

Entrepreneurship. We encourage people to set their own direction. We are looking for senior engineers who can lead product decisions. All engineers are able to suggest, research, and lead architectural changes, contribute to and suggest revisions to our roadmap, and create new coding guidelines and have them be enforced.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

title: Firebase is hiring operations engineers in SF
text:
At Firebase, we're building the first realtime database-as-a-service. Every other database was designed to be downloaded and run on a business's own servers behind a firewall. Firebase is different -- it's a cloud service that's managed directly by the people who make it.

By centralizing operations in the hands of our team, we can provide a superior experience for our developers, increased reliability, and massive efficiencies of scale. Our small team already manages the databases for 10s of thousands of developers.

We need some smart, creative, and disciplined operations engineers to take our infrastructure to the next level. The ideal candidate would have: (1) a keen attention to detail (2) strong programming skills (3) a solid working knowledge of Linux (4) a drive to automate things

This will be a fun job for the right person. We work at serious scale and we have a tight knit team of talented folks. What's more, you'll be handling operations for a product you'll help design and build, rather than simply running someone else's software on your servers. You'll be joining the 24x7 on-call rotation and day to day tasks will align with maximizing the uptime of the Firebase production environment. Switching between the OS, network concerns, and deployed application details will be common place in this role.

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to. We also work at serious scale. To this end, as part of the ops team you'll be in close contact with making sure everything is running smoothly for our developer-centric customers. You'll get to work on a deployment of physical hardware on the path to our globally-distributed, multi-datacenter operations.

title: Data scientist @ Scribd: Found our data team (SF)
text:
Scribd is looking for a deeply analytical person to help us make sense of the wealth of data pouring into our servers. As the founding member of our data team, you will have broad ownership of data across the site - from financial to user behavior data. You'll be the front-line for people with questions about how various parts of the site are doing and will be in a position to unlock huge amounts of business value by spotting important trends.

Because of our unique subscription model, Scribd is perhaps the first company in the history of the book business to have extensive data not just on what books people buy, but on exactly what parts of a book they actually read. We plan to use this opportunity to draw unprecedented insights into reading behavior.

Here are some examples of the kinds of data questions we want to explore:

• What makes a good book recommendation? What signals can we use to do a better job recommending books?

• What insights can we provide to authors and publishers about what parts of their books are being read that will help them to write better books?

• How can we build a model to predict how valuable a set of books are to help us decide what content to acquire?

• What factors determine whether a user stays and engages with the product? How can we optimize the experience to delight every new user and keep them reading?

Our Ideal Candidate Has

• Highly developed quantitative skills, as evidenced by a degree in a technical field like math, physics, or computer science; or equivalent work experience

• Great SQL skills: you are a database whiz

• A strong business understanding: you aren’t satisfied with surface analysis, but drill down into data looking for what is “really” going on

• Great communication skills and the ability to translate general and under-specified goals into precise questions

• Development skills with one or more major programming languages

About Us

Scribd (YC S'06), based in San Francisco, is building the world's online library. Scribd has raised $26M, is profitable, and is one of the largest sites on the web with over 80M monthly users, but it is still run by a comparatively small team and still in the very early stages of achieving our vision for what the library of the future could be. We recently launched a subscription service that is widely being called the first “Netflix for books” and we’re very excited about it.

Applying

Just email us at jobs@scribd.com with "Data Scientist" in the subject. The founders review and respond to all resumes within 24 hours. We'd love to hear from you!

title: Firebase is hiring operations engineers in SF
text:
At Firebase, we're building the first realtime database-as-a-service. Every other database was designed to be downloaded and run on a business's own servers behind a firewall. Firebase is different -- it's a cloud service that's managed directly by the people who make it.

By centralizing operations in the hands of our team, we can provide a superior experience for our developers, increased reliability, and massive efficiencies of scale. Our small team already manages the databases for 10s of thousands of developers.

We need some smart, creative, and disciplined operations engineers to take our infrastructure to the next level. The ideal candidate would have: (1) a keen attention to detail (2) strong programming skills (3) a solid working knowledge of Linux (4) a drive to automate things

This will be a fun job for the right person. We work at serious scale and we have a tight knit team of talented folks. What's more, you'll be handling operations for a product you'll help design and build, rather than simply running someone else's software on your servers. You'll be joining the 24x7 on-call rotation and day to day tasks will align with maximizing the uptime of the Firebase production environment. Switching between the OS, network concerns, and deployed application details will be common place in this role.

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to. We also work at serious scale. To this end, as part of the ops team you'll be in close contact with making sure everything is running smoothly for our developer-centric customers. You'll get to work on a deployment of physical hardware on the path to our globally-distributed, multi-datacenter operations.

Second, we care a lot about cultivating a great work environment. This is our happy place. We're friendly people, we have a light-weight engineering process, and we have a sweet 3 story penthouse office in SoMa.

Third, you can have a big impact here. We're a small team (but growing very quickly), and you'll have a big say in the direction of the company. And, since we're serious about changing the way software is built, you could have a big impact on the way all software is made. We won't stop until the "refresh" button is a thing of the past.

If you're interested, send us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

title: GinzaMetrics is Hiring Developers to Improve Search and Content Marketing
text:

Because we're a fully distributed team, we place a high value on communication, responsiveness and autonomy. We're a hard-working team and we solve bigger problems than our small team size would seem capable of solving. Our business is growing quickly and our #1 goal is to make our customers happy every day.

We don't provide everyone with massages or an unlimited supply of kale chips, nor do we distract ourselves with ping pong tables or video games. But, being a distributed team gives us the flexibility to choose our own working environments, meet up in interesting locales, and serve an international market from anywhere we choose. So whether you're into kale or kegs, you can do as you please while managing your workload and location. We can promise that you'll be challenged every day.

Our stack / tools:

- Ruby / Rails

- MySQL / PostgreSQL

- Cassandra

- JavaScript

- jQuery

- Angular.js

- Highcharts

- D3.js

- Amazon S3

- Lots of APIs (ad networks, social networks, etc.)

- Redis

- Resque

- Github

- Memcache

- Chef

- Jenkins

Technical Requirements:

We're looking for mid- to senior level, full-stack developers with experience in Ruby on Rails or similar environment (experience in other languages and frameworks such as Python / Python frameworks is fine, but we're not going to rewrite things in your favorite language)

- Strong understanding and experience with UNIX / Linux tools and concepts

- Familiar with web application security principles / encryption best practices

- Ability to ramp up in our environment and be productive in 1 week (we provide a comprehensive ramping-up guide)

- Solid understanding and experience in SQL and SQL optimization (indexes, queries, write-read performance, etc.)

- Solid understanding of NoSQL principles and tradeoffs

- Solid understanding of distributed systems / architectures

Bonus / really great to have:

- Understanding / experience with large-scale ETL

- Understanding / experience with OLAP (we don't use MDX, etc. but understanding this sort of model will help you adapt to our platform quickly)

- Experience with Cassandra, Storm, Kafka and / or similar tools

- Experience with web crawling, text mining and headless browser automation

Other Requirements:

- Fanaticism about our market and our product

- Ability / willingness to quickly ramp up on our industry and become an expert in the field

- Courage

- Ability to communicate well and make recommendations in the context of an overall set of possible solutions, with benefits / tradeoffs for each

- Humility towards team members, hubris towards opportunity

- Self-starter

Website:

www.ginzametrics.com

Email us your LinkedIn URL and github profile (if you have any open source code or contributions) at hackers@ginzametrics.com.

title: Firebase (YC S11) is hiring core developers in Seattle
text:
Are you a developer in the Seattle area with experience building databases, high performance networking, or distributed systems? We want to hear from you.

At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only between servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier. Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

Over 500,000 devices are connected to Firebase's servers at any given time, and 10s of millions of users use a Firebase-powered app every day.

Our team is serious about computer science as a discipline -- we have folks hailing from Mozilla, Google, Microsoft, Twitter, HP, Adobe, Akamai, and Adroll -- but WE NEED YOU to take Firebase to the next level. We tackle some of the hardest problems in computer science every day: large distributed systems, data merging and conflict resolution, data security, language design, high performance networking, index generation, etc.

If you're interested, please drop us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

We save consumers money on groceries by partnering with big manufacturers and retail chains. Shoppers buy our offers and subscriptions through web and mobile for 15% to 50% off of normal prices. We then load those items to the shopper’s store loyalty card. When shoppers checkout at the grocery store, they receive full credit for items they already bought on Aisle50. Manufacturers pay the difference between our prices and retail, plus a fee to Aisle50 for marketing and facilitating the back-end technology that allows for the conversion consumers before they ever get to the store shelf.

Our solution is unique in that it melds the brick and mortar world of grocery stores with the web. We alter shopping behavior in a powerful way: we drive extra trips to the store and, once the consumer is at the store, we drive shopping baskets that are 31% bigger for our retail partners.

Some of our manufacturer clients: Kellogg’s, Procter & Gamble, Unilever, General Mills, PepsiCo.

Some of our retailers: Raley’s, Shop ‘n Save, Homeland, D’Agostino, Foodland, Jubilee.

About you:

Right now, Aisle50 offers an iOS app and optimized views to its users, but with our current team’s focus on the evolution of the webapp and our live connections with retailers, the mobile half does not get the attention it deserves. You will change that.

You will have experience building mobile applications from the ground-up. You will lead the effort to create the next generation of Aisle50 mobile offerings as well as help vendor our code for use by our grocery partners, some of whom have their own mobile apps that can utilize modular pieces of our solution.

We already own the consumer outside of the store as that’s where we reach them; but we want to own the consumer inside the store as well. That means integrating mobile with location-based solutions that allow us to communicate with our shoppers at critical moments in the brick-and-mortar buying funnel, from when the shopper enters the store to when the shopper browses the bread aisle to when the shopper checks out this week’s gossip magazine in the checkout line (we work with Time Inc.!).

Our strategy involves both iOS and Android and we would love to find someone with deep knowledge of both, but we're excited to meet people who are stronger in one or the other as well. Bonus points if you have some Rails experience and can work on the APIs the app will consume as well as the app itself.

You will be joining a dev team of 4 + 2 cofounders + 8 sales people + 1 customer service specialist. We roll fast, so you should, too.

Interested? Email us at mobilejob@aisle50.com

title: Firebase (YC S11) is hiring core developers in SF
text:
At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only between servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier. Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

Over 500,000 devices are connected to Firebase's servers at any given time, and 10s of millions of users use a Firebase-powered app every day.

Our team is serious about computer science as a discipline -- we have folks hailing from Mozilla, Google, Microsoft, Twitter, HP, Adobe, Akamai, and Adroll -- but WE NEED YOU to take Firebase to the next level. We tackle some of the hardest problems in computer science every day: large distributed systems, data merging and conflict resolution, data security, language design, high performance networking, index generation, etc.

If you've previously worked on the internals of databases, spent time optimizing network stacks, or if you feel you're an especially strong algorithms programmer, please drop us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

title: Panorama Education: Full-Stack Engineer, Class of 2014 or starting immediately
Firebase is hiring core devs. Help us reinvent the database
text:
At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only be servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier.

Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

We're making some bold claims, and we need some bold engineers to help us build this future. We're especially interested in people with strong algorithms backgrounds. If you've previously worked on the internals of databases, you've spent time optimizing networking stacks, or if you feel you're an especially strong algorithms programmer, give us a shout!

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to. So, while every startup says they have hard technical challenges, we really do. You'll get to design new synchronization algorithms, invent new languages, use cool new data structures, optimize network stacks, and more.

Second, we care a lot about cultivating a great work environment. This is our happy place. We're friendly people, we have a light-weight engineering process, and we have a sweet 3 story penthouse office in SoMa.

Third, you can have a big impact here. We're a small team (but growing very quickly), and you'll have a big say in the direction of the company. And, since we're serious about changing the way software is built, you could have a big impact on the way all software is made. We won't stop until the "refresh" button is a thing of the past.

If you're interested, send us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

title: Help Build APIs for Commercial Banking
text:
Opportunity

Standard Treasury builds software for banks. That might seem boring, but everyone uses a bank and we dream of making their technology simple, beautiful, and intuitive. Think about your online banking system with its outdated, unpleasant UI and UX — we’re working to fix that. To get some idea of the market: U.S. banks spend $400 billion dollar per year on IT.

See http://techcrunch.com/2013/07/09/standard-treasury/ for some more information.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Product

Our first product is a white-labeled API interface and developer experience that we’ll sell to banks. Our technology enables banks to programmatically offer their services to their clients using modern, RESTful APIs. From here we plan on expanding into desktop online banking, mobile banking, and core banking (the systems that record teller transactions, and how much money everyone has in their bank accounts).

Traction

We have significant traction on our API product with several top-25 banks. The price points of these contracts range from $1 million to over $5 million per year. With these contract sizes and a growing customer base; we have an opportunity to avoid any significant equity dilution with a traditional fundraising round.

Team

We are a small team based in San Francisco focused on unsexy but incredibly valuable services that will change the face of banking and we are looking for the right people to join us. We are building a team of excellent people who work hard and don’t tolerate bullshit. We want passionate partners who share our desire to shake up banking software. We practice internal transparency a la Stripe (http://bit.ly/VSv54h) and corporate candor.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Compensation and Perks

You can expect:

1. Great benefits. Medical, vision, and dental insurance for you and your dependents.

2. Great comp. Salary and equity. Critically, we’re interested in finding the right balance for you. We know there are some people who have a greater risk appetite than others.

3. Great perks. Free lunch and dinner, snacks, a stocked fridge, laundry service, gym membership, Clipper card, house cleaning by Exec or Homejoy, and delivery errands by Postmates.

4. Great flexibility. (a) Flexible hours. So that you can live your life. (b) Open vacation policy. We all need to recharge. We mean it — there is a two week minimum and we’ll send you home in December if we have to. (c) Paid maternity and paternity leave.

5. Great tools. Build your ideal workstations so you can have the tools you want and need. Buy the books you need or want on Amazon. Need a Kindle for your commute — get it. The corporate Amex can be used for all expenses under a standard of trust & reasonableness.

Roles

We are hiring as quickly as we can find good people in a large number of roles.

1. Platform and APIs. For those who think they can build something as beautiful and durable as Twilio, Stripe, or Facebook Connect.

2. UI, UX, and design. This will start with easy-to-use API documentation and intuitive websites. In the future it will expand into the future of online (and mobile) banking.

3. Bank integrations. Half our job is taking pre-modern internal banking systems and making them disappear for our users. This requires patience and, fortunately or unfortunately, a deep love of puzzles.

4. Systems and security. We integrate with some of the most sensitive and secure systems in the world. We need to be even better. A security breach will kill our company.

5. Define your own role. Let us know what you want to work on to disrupt banking software.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

title: Firebase is hiring core devs. Help us reinvent the database
text:
At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only be servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier.

Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

We're making some bold claims, and we need some bold engineers to help us build this future. We're especially interested in people with strong algorithms backgrounds. If you've previously worked on the internals of databases, you've spent time optimizing networking stacks, or if you feel you're an especially strong algorithms programmer, give us a shout!

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to. So, while every startup says they have hard technical challenges, we really do. You'll get to design new synchronization algorithms, invent new languages, use cool new data structures, optimize network stacks, and more.

Second, we care a lot about cultivating a great work environment. This is our happy place. We're friendly people, we have a light-weight engineering process, and we have a sweet 3 story penthouse office in SoMa.

Third, you can have a big impact here. We're a small team (but growing very quickly), and you'll have a big say in the direction of the company. And, since we're serious about changing the way software is built, you could have a big impact on the way all software is made. We won't stop until the "refresh" button is a thing of the past.

If you're interested, send us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

title: MongoHQ (YC S11) is hiring a marketing brain
text:
We are a Series A funded database infrastructure company with significant revenue and an enviable customer list. We're also not very good at marketing, and are fortunate to have grown almost entirely due to word of mouth referrals and a relentless commitment to customer support. It's time we got better at getting our message out there, and we're looking for someone to make that happen.

You might be a good person to own this problem if you are an experienced marketer with hacking skills, or a really good hacker with marketing experience. If you are good at creating a consistent voice and infusing a group of smart people with a "marketing identity" you have a good foundation to work from.

High quality content is (so far) the most effective way to reach our audience. We would desperately like to talk to you if you know how to build a machine that helps us consistently create and deliver content developers want. Content, in our context, is everything from published writing to presentations to open source projects. If you can expand the scope of "good marketing to developers" to be more than just content, even better.

The actual scope of the job could range from "first dedicated marketing hire" to "VP of Marketing", it totally depends on the person. Our investors want us to start with a battle hardened marketing VP, but we like to experiment and may do it differently. What we really want is a get-shit-done type who will build marketing capabilities into our company with a healthy combination of tools, metrics, processes and people (when necessary).

Our ideal customers (developers) are something of a unique market, and we are determined to make sure our company continues to interact with them in a healthy way. If you are interested in helping us build this area of our business, send an email to hello@mongohq.com with an example of how you'd approach developers if you were us ... and if you're brave ... challenge some of our assumptions (read on).

Boilerplate: we have offices in San Mateo, CA and Birmingham AL, with remote employees in London, two cities in Canada and Utah. We offer competitive benefits including an open vacation policy, individual technology budgets, and a comprehensive medical plan.

Assumptions: We have beliefs about the way the world works, where it's going, and what it means for our business. We're also a little bit overprotective of developers. Here are some assumptions that we frequently use to shape decisions:

Number 1: Developers are the most influential technology decision makers in many companies, and will soon be the most influential in every company. We should help developers achieve this utopia.

Number 2: Enterprise is changing and we are in the exciting early days of crazy self service. In the future, most companies will buy technology without directly interacting with a human. The extreme example of this is AWS, we spend 6 figures per month on Amazon's Cloud Services and would prefer not to talk to a sales person. We should position ourselves in a way that prepares us for this future.

Number 3: Our customers and not-yet customers are continuously inundated with shameless corporate promotion and crap messaging. This is not ok. We should give them something with value that compensates for the intrusiveness of how we're reaching them. If we're speaking to people who are already customers, teaching them how to solve problems with our product is valuable. If we're speaking to not-yet customers, we should leave them with some no-strings-attached knowledge they can use on their own.

We'd love to hear from you. Write to: hello@mongohq.com.

Manager/Director, Digital Marketing at GetGoing
text:
About GetGoing

GetGoing is a travel technology company creating a radically better discovery, shopping and booking experience for leisure and corporate travelers. Our team of travel industry veterans and e-commerce, marketing, and data science experts is delivering a bold new vision of how travel should be sold in the 21st century. For consumers, this means lower prices, better selection, and intuitive, personalized search. For suppliers, it’s about being able to differentiate their products and market profitably to more customers.

We have partnered with many of the world’s leading airlines, hotel chains, Global Distribution Systems and Travel Management Companies to build a better way of marketing and selling travel products online.

We operate two lines of business:

• Online Travel Agency: GetGoing.com is an award-winning discovery, search and booking platform for flights and hotels. Powered by patented search and revenue management technology, we are able to offer discounts on flights and hotel nights not available anywhere else. GetGoing.com is currently live in the United States, and will be available internationally soon.

• Travel content distribution: We provide a worldwide platform connecting airline and hotel suppliers with leisure and corporate travel agencies and ad networks for the distribution of rich media travel content. Our platform enables partners to showcase their products to consumers and significantly increase customer loyalty and conversion. GetGoing is backed by leading consumer internet venture capital and private equity funds and is based in San Francisco. We graduated from Y Combinator’s S12 class.

About the Role

We are looking for a Digital Marketing Manager / Director to help us define and execute our digital marketing strategy. We have grown largely organically since we launched 6 months ago, and the time is right to fire up the engines.

We are looking for someone who can operate effectively at a start-up, work with a limited budget, be comfortable with limited oversight, but enjoy having plenty of product, design and technical support. You have creative ideas, and you are not afraid to try them.

You know digital marketing inside out. PPC, SEM, display advertising, retargeting, and landing page optimization. You know what these words mean both practically & theoretically. You know how to set ambitious goals, you know where to start, and know how to deliver results on a start-up schedule. If you also know something about off-line advertising, branding, e-mail and content strategy, you would be one in a million – definitely mention that when we meet.

If you come in for an interview, we will ask you a simple question: “Where do we start?” Some of us will want a detailed answer, some will want to hear the big picture. If you can answer this question clearly, intelligently, and logically, we will ask when you can start.

We ask for a lot:

• A degree from a top-tier school or a record of extraordinary accomplishment in some endeavor. The type of endeavor doesn’t matter. Ability & desire to push to win does. Winning matters a lot more than a good school.

• 4+ years of digital marketing experience. Less is more if you paid your way through college doing this stuff or can otherwise convince us that you’ve mastered both the big-picture stuff and the granular details of digital marketing.

• Investment banking level modeling & analytics skills. If you are not there, tell us how you will get there. As you know, analytics matters, and we don’t have a separate department doing that.

• Experience managing vendors & partners effectively. That’s a polite way of saying: you know who to talk to and how to get a deal.

• Comfort with technology – we are a technology company, and you need to be able to explain what you need to tech people. If you can explain things well, your projects will always get in front of the line.

• You are an entrepreneur by nature. The word means a lot. You are a dreamer. You are a doer. You would rather try and fail than not try at all. You don’t sit around waiting for directions. You always have your own opinion. The list goes on, but we spot them when they walk in the door.

• You have a favorite place where you book travel, and can tell us why you book there. There are no right or wrong answers.

• You like the travel industry – note that this is very different from liking travel. We will ask you to explain the difference between an OTA, a TMC, a GDS, and a meta-search and you are either already familiar with the industry or have read up enough before the interview to have an intelligent discussion.

We offer a lot:

• A unique opportunity to play an integral role in building a consumer travel brand. We are developing technologies that can flip a trillion dollar industry on its head. You heard it right. A trillion. You have to enjoy being in a very crowded space though

• You will be joining a very well funded start-up very early on. Not on the ground floor, but we are building a skyscraper – you’ll do very well.

• We offer a good salary. Google & Facebook pay better, but you don’t want to be at Google or Facebook. You want to blaze your own trail, not follow in someone else’s footsteps. You want to join before the IPO. Way before the IPO.

• Getting to work is easy – we are next door to Caltrain – literally next door – you can see the train numbers from the roof. We are a few blocks from BART. Many of us bike to work. If you don’t bike, we offer monthly commuter / parking expense reimbursement. If you do bike, we take care of your bike.

• We want you to stay fit. Membership at the San Francisco Tennis Club is deeply subsidized – it’s a block away, so there is no excuse. Literally a block away. There are tennis balls on the roof. You can also bike to the Bay Club if you like yoga and swimming better than tennis.

• We feed you well. Breakfast, lunch, dinner, midnight snacks. All organic, no MSG. If you don’t like organic, that’s OK too, we’ll get you a separate bunch of oranges. Pesticides are cheaper, and we are a frugal bunch.

• Vacation is unlimited. Deliver outstanding results, and you get to do it from Hawaii or Mt. Everest, your call.

title: Thalmic (YC W13) is hiring a PM
Firebase is hiring core devs. Help us reinvent the database
text:
At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database. Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only be servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier.

Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

We're making some bold claims, and we need some bold engineers to help us build this future. We're especially interested in people with strong algorithms backgrounds. If you've previously worked on the internals of databases, you've spent time optimizing networking stacks, or if you feel you're an especially strong algorithms programmer, give us a shout!

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to. So, while every startup says they have hard technical challenges, we really do. You'll get to design new synchronization algorithms, invent new languages, use cool new data structures, optimize network stacks, and more.

Second, we care a lot about cultivating a great work environment. This is our happy place. We're friendly people, we have a light-weight engineering process, and we have a sweet 3 story penthouse office in SoMa.

Third, you can have a big impact here. We're a small team (but growing very quickly), and you'll have a big say in the direction of the company. And, since we're serious about changing the way software is built, you could have a big impact on the way all software is made. We won't stop until the "refresh" button is a thing of the past.

If you're interested, send us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html
