title: Be Engineer #1 at Padlet and simplify how everyday people use the Internet
text:
Padlet (padlet.com), a YCombinator and Imagine K12 backed company, is looking for its first engineer (employee #1 if you will).

At Padlet we are making an online version of paper, an extremely simple way to put and share stuff on the Internet. We already have hundreds of thousands of users in over 200 countries (yup, we have users in Mongolia!). We are venture funded and growing fast. We have been called the next Tumblr, the next Google Docs, and even the next Twitter.

There are, of course, a gazillion startups looking for engineers. You can pick any and you'll do well in life. So WHY PADLET? Besides all the bells and whistles of every single startup these days (a.k.a 'unlimited' vacation + choose your own workstation + be your own boss etc), here is what's good about us:

- Actually generous equity. Much, much more than an average Bay Area startup, particularly considering how successful the company already is.

- We're solving an important problem - making it easy for each and every person to put stuff on the Internet. It's something your grandmom can use. People are using us at work, in schools, at home, and even in police stations. Padlet is the first software ever used by a group of refugee kids in Australia. Making software for such an audience is difficult but rewarding. It also means you may have to explain to some users what it means to "Copy & Paste".

- All of our tremendous growth has been organic. We've proven that people really want our product. Search for "padlet" on twitter to see what we mean. This also means we don't talk about social media or email newsletter strategy. We just focus on building an awesome product.

- We do crazy things like coding on a train from San Francisco to Portland (and even getting pizza delivered to the Sacramento station to satisfy late night munchies).

- We're post-traction, post-revenue, and have exceptional investors. Yet we are tiny in size. If you ever wanted to run and grow a company but founding one wasn't your cup of tea, Padlet is perfect for you.

WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

- Good sense of humor

- Honesty, Humility, Hard Work (look ma, alliteration)

- Impressive past or current projects (Open Source contributions or otherwise). We don't really care what languages/platforms you have used before but we definitely prefer those who have full-stack web and/or mobile development experience.

- Good sense of humor

TO APPLY, email us at imgood@padlet.com with whatever you'd like us to know. Bonus points if you include a fun hackathon idea in your email. We are based in San Francisco but open to hiring anywhere in the world (this includes the ISS).

--

Love, laughter

The Folks at Padlet

p.s. If you already have your dream job, please pass this on to someone you admire.

Our team of travel industry veterans and e-commerce, marketing, and data science experts is delivering a bold new vision of how travel should be sold in the 21st century. For suppliers, it’s about being able to differentiate their products and market profitably to more customers.

We operate two lines of business:

GetGoing.com is currently live in the United States, and will be available internationally soon.

Our platform enables partners to showcase their products to consumers and significantly increase customer loyalty and conversion.

GetGoing is backed by leading consumer internet venture capital and private equity funds and is based in San Francisco. We graduated from Y Combinator’s S12 class.

We are looking for a Digital Marketing Manager / Director to help us define and execute our digital marketing strategy. We have grown largely organically since we launched 6 months ago, and the time is right to fire up the engines.

We are looking for someone who can operate effectively at a start-up, work with a limited budget, be comfortable with limited oversight, but enjoy having plenty of product, design and technical support. You have creative ideas, and you are not afraid to try them.

You know digital marketing inside out. PPC, SEM, display advertising, retargeting, and landing page optimization. You know what these words mean both practically & theoretically. You know how to set ambitious goals, you know where to start, and know how to deliver results on a start-up schedule. If you also know something about off-line advertising, branding, e-mail and content strategy, you would be one in a million – definitely mention that when we meet.

If you come in for an interview, we will ask you a simple question: “Where do we start?” Some of us will want a detailed answer, some will want to hear the big picture. If you can answer this question clearly, intelligently, and logically, we will ask when you can start.

We ask for a lot:

• A degree from a top-tier school or a record of extraordinary accomplishment in some endeavor. The type of endeavor doesn’t matter. Ability & desire to push to win does. Winning matters a lot more than a good school.

• 4+ years of digital marketing experience. Less is more if you paid your way through college doing this stuff or can otherwise convince us that you’ve mastered both the big-picture stuff and the granular details of digital marketing.

• Investment banking level modeling & analytics skills. If you are not there, tell us how you will get there. As you know, analytics matters, and we don’t have a separate department doing that.

• Experience managing vendors & partners effectively. That’s a polite way of saying: you know who to talk to and how to get a deal.

• Comfort with technology – we are a technology company, and you need to be able to explain what you need to tech people. If you can explain things well, your projects will always get in front of the line.

• You are an entrepreneur by nature. The word means a lot. You are a dreamer. You are a doer. You would rather try and fail than not try at all. You don’t sit around waiting for directions. You always have your own opinion. The list goes on, but we spot them when they walk in the door.

• You have a favorite place where you book travel, and can tell us why you book there. There are no right or wrong answers.

• You like the travel industry – note that this is very different from liking travel. We will ask you to explain the difference between an OTA, a TMC, a GDS, and a meta-search and you are either already familiar with the industry or have read up enough before the interview to have an intelligent discussion.

We offer a lot:

• A unique opportunity to play an integral role in building a consumer travel brand. We are developing technologies that can flip a trillion dollar industry on its head. You heard it right. A trillion. You have to enjoy being in a very crowded space though

• You will be joining a very well funded start-up very early on. Not on the ground floor, but we are building a skyscraper – you’ll do very well.

• We offer a good salary. Google & Facebook pay better, but you don’t want to be at Google or Facebook. You want to blaze your own trail, not follow in someone else’s footsteps. You want to join before the IPO. Way before the IPO.

• Getting to work is easy – we are next door to Caltrain – literally next door – you can see the train numbers from the roof. We are a few blocks from BART. Many of us bike to work. If you don’t bike, we offer monthly commuter / parking expense reimbursement. If you do bike, we take care of your bike.

• We want you to stay fit. Membership at the San Francisco Tennis Club is deeply subsidized – it’s a block away, so there is no excuse. Literally a block away. There are tennis balls on the roof. You can also bike to the Bay Club if you like yoga and swimming better than tennis.

• We feed you well. Breakfast, lunch, dinner, midnight snacks. All organic, no MSG. If you don’t like organic, that’s OK too, we’ll get you a separate bunch of oranges. Pesticides are cheaper, and we are a frugal bunch.

• Vacation is unlimited. Deliver outstanding results, and you get to do it from Hawaii or Mt. Everest, your call.

To apply for this position, please email your resume to jobs@getgoing.com with the subject line "Manager/Director, Digital Marketing".

title: Standard Treasury is scaling fast to change how companies use their banks
text:
Opportunity

Standard Treasury builds software for banks. That might seem boring, but everyone uses a bank and we dream of making their technology simple, beautiful, and intuitive. Think about your online banking system with its outdated, unpleasant UI and UX — we’re working to fix that. To get some idea of the market: U.S. banks spend $400 billion dollar per year on IT.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Product

Our first product is a white-labeled API interface and developer experience that we’ll sell to banks. Our technology enables banks to programmatically offer their services to their clients using modern, RESTful APIs. From here we plan on expanding into desktop online banking, mobile banking, and core banking (the systems that record teller transactions, and how much money everyone has in their bank accounts).

Traction

We have significant traction on our API product with several top-25 banks. The price points of these contracts range from $1 million to over $5 million per year. With these contract sizes and a growing customer base; we have an opportunity to avoid any significant equity dilution with a traditional fundraising round.

Team

We are a six person team based in San Francisco focused on unsexy but incredibly valuable services that will change the face of banking and we are looking for the right people to join us. We are building a team of excellent people (current team is from Facebook, Microsoft, Disqus, Sidecar, Stripe) who work hard and don’t tolerate bullshit. We want passionate partners who share our desire to shake up banking software. We practice internal transparency a la Stripe (http://bit.ly/VSv54h) and corporate candor.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Compensation and Perks

You can expect:

1. Great benefits. Medical, vision, and dental insurance for you and your dependents.

2. Great comp. Salary and equity. Critically, we’re interested in finding the right balance for you. We know there are some people who have a greater risk appetite than others.

3. Great perks. Free lunch and dinner, snacks, a stocked fridge, laundry service, gym membership, Clipper card, and house cleaning by Homejoy. We're also open to suggestions for anything that can let you focus on the things you care about.

4. Great flexibility. (a) Flexible hours. So that you can live your life. (b) Open vacation policy. We all need to recharge. We mean it — there is a two week minimum and we’ll send you home in December if we have to. (c) Paid maternity and paternity leave.

5. Great tools. Build your ideal workstations so you can have the tools you want and need. Buy the books you need or want on Amazon. Need a Kindle for your commute — get it. The corporate Amex can be used for all expenses under a standard of trust & reasonableness.

Roles

We are hiring as quickly as we can find good people in a large number of roles.

1. Platform and APIs. For those who think they can build something as beautiful and durable as Twilio, Stripe, or Facebook Connect.

2. UI, UX, and design. This will start with easy-to-use API documentation and intuitive websites. In the future it will expand into the future of online (and mobile) banking.

3. Bank integrations. Half our job is taking pre-modern internal banking systems and making them disappear for our users. This requires patience and, fortunately or unfortunately, a deep love of puzzles.

4. Systems and security. We integrate with some of the most sensitive and secure systems in the world. We need to be even better. A security breach will kill our company.

5. Define your own role. Let us know what you want to work on to disrupt banking software.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

title: ZeroCater is Hiring Hackers
Aisle50 (YC S11) is hiring a mobile dev in Chicago
text:
# What We Do

Aisle50 enables consumers to save on groceries while helping bricks-and-mortar grocery retailers battle the encroachment of big box stores and Amazon. Our sales team sources offers directly from manufacturers, and we pass those savings (often 30-60% off) to the shopper through our website.

Shoppers love us because our offers are easy to use and provide much bigger savings than typical coupons—sometimes more than $10 at a time.

Manufacturers love us because our programs are cheap and easy to execute—printing paper coupons is expensive. We give manufacturers the opportunity to make the sale before the customer ever gets to the store. It’s a strategy that works: 80-90% of people who buy Aisle50 offers haven't bought the product in the previous three months, so we're truly introducing the product to new people—the ultimate goal of the manufacturer.

Grocery stores love us because we drive trips to the store and, much like gift cards drive extra spending beyond the value of the cards, consumers spend more at the store when they redeem Aisle50 offers.

# Why We're Hiring

Mobile is growing and important part of grocery. Not everybody in the store has a smartphone, but nobody has a desktop. We have a mobile-optimized site and a lightweight native app now, but we want to provide an awesome customer experience in the store and we need more robust mobile apps to do it.

Things we want to do in mobile:

* Put out slick mobile solutions that keep pace with our ever-evolving webapp. * Integrate a UPC scanner to make it easy for people to know whether an item is included in our offers. (Our largest in-store issue occurs when consumers grab the wrong items) * As we get tighter with our retailer partners, we need to be able to package our mobile offerings within the apps belonging to retailers, something that will require thorough knowledge in mobile development. * We’d like to integrate with solutions that allow us to locate a consumer within the store to keep the right messages, alerts and offers in front of them.

# Who We're Hiring

* Likely 4-6 years experience writing software, with 1-2 years in mobile * Both iOS and Android experience would be excellent, but we know that’s a tall order. We’re excited to talk to candidates with core strength in one of them. * Bonus for Rails experience, as it would be a plus if candidate can work on APIs the app will consume as well as the app itself

Our current team has limited mobile experience, so we need someone who brings that as a strength. You won't be entirely on your own - we'll be able to pick up the languages pretty fast. But with any technology, the environment and tooling is one of the biggest hurdles. We need someone who knows how to set up a project from scratch, pull in the right libraries, and create a solid foundation that is going to work for us long-term. Since we’ll be vendoring code to our grocery partners as well as shipping our own native apps that foundation will need to be highly modular as well.

# What It's Like Here

Aisle50 currently has 15 employees (see http://aisle50.com/team). All the devs work with and report directly to the co-founders.

We believe in the paramount importance of the customer experience. We have a number of constituencies, so walking the line between what's good for shoppers, manufacturers, and retailers is a difficult but rewarding daily challenge. We're humble about our code. We try to mitigate risk by taking small steps and creating safety nets (eg: test-driven development, continuous integration).

Our process is inspired by Agile and Kanban but with such a small team we're pragmatic about doing what works. We have a weekly meeting and a morning check-in to make sure we aren't losing focus. In and out of those meetings we talk with each other about what we're working on, what's important, and how to solve problems. We're all responsible for actively improving the company and the product. Developers' ideas are consistently being knit into our products.

We eat lunch together every day. It's not required or anything, we just like each other :)

# Stack

Our current tools include:

Rails

Ruby

heroku

postgres

mailgun

S3

rackspace (we need a static IP for some of our retailer integrations)

rspec

*json API

We develop on Macbook Pros, 24-inch monitors and faux-wood IKEA desks. We all use different editors.

The job is in Chicago. Interested? Email us at mobilejob@aisle50.com

title: Firebase is hiring core devs. Help us reinvent the database
text:
At Firebase, we're completely reinventing the database.

Every database to date has been built using a request / response paradigm, and it has been intended for use only be servers on a local network. Firebase is different. It's built to be accessed directly from client devices, and it uses a real-time synchronization approach that makes building modern applications radically easier.

Firebase-powered apps can be written in a fraction of the time, require only client-side code, update in real-time out-of-the-box, and scale automatically.

We're making some bold claims, and we need some bold engineers to help us build this future. We're especially interested in people with strong algorithms backgrounds. If you've previously worked on the internals of databases, you've spent time optimizing networking stacks, or if you feel you're an especially strong algorithms programmer, give us a shout!

Why should you join Firebase?

First, we're one of the few small companies who are tackling tough computer science problems on a daily basis. We're in the business of handling the hard technical aspects of real-time data sync so that our customers don't have to. So, while every startup says they have hard technical challenges, we really do. You'll get to design new synchronization algorithms, invent new languages, use cool new data structures, optimize network stacks, and more.

Second, we care a lot about cultivating a great work environment. This is our happy place. We're friendly people, we have a light-weight engineering process, and we have a sweet 3 story penthouse office in SoMa.

Third, you can have a big impact here. We're a small team (but growing very quickly), and you'll have a big say in the direction of the company. And, since we're serious about changing the way software is built, you could have a big impact on the way all software is made. We won't stop until the "refresh" button is a thing of the past.

If you're interested, send us an email at jobs@firebase.com.

You can see more about our open positions here: https://www.firebase.com/jobs.html

title: Matterport (YC W12) enables you to make online 3D copies of physical places
text:

We have an initial version of our product in beta with large companies in home improvement, real estate, construction, and insurance, and things are going very well. You can check out what our reconstructions look like at http://matterport.com/explore/ Our vision is to provide an end-to-end solution for not just capturing but also publishing, sharing, and transforming real-world 3D data online.

We’ve raised a good bit of cash ($7.2m in total), and we're now working hard to deliver the production version of our product later this year. Our total team is 19 people right now, and we're poised to do a good bit of hiring in the next few months. We’re large enough that you’re coming in to a well-organized team with great tools and a lot of support but small enough that your individual contribution will be crucial to our product’s success. We’re also large enough that we can pay you a good salary but small enough that we can give you a significant chunk of equity.

We're proud to be creating something incredibly useful. This is going to become a vital tool for the millions of professionals who work with 3D spaces on a daily basis, including real estate companies, remodelers, insurance companies, construction companies, building operators, architects, retail designers, and more. Our customers are excited and clamoring to buy our production cameras as soon as they are available.

---

A bit about us:

We are all experienced founders and were previously early employees at PayPal and Google. We like to work hard and get shit done. We are intellectual and curious. We know how to communicate and get along. We're goofy and keep the work atmosphere fun.

Most of all, though, we're driven to change the world in a deep and meaningful way.

We’re looking to fill the following positions right now: - Backend web developer: You’ll be responsible for the cloud computing infrastructure for processing our models. We currently make heavy use of Amazon’s cloud computing stack, and use Django for our web backend. - Software developer with 3D web experience: You’ll be responsible for the way people experience our 3D models online. We’re currently using Unity, but are looking at WebGL as a medium term alternative. - Software engineer with computer vision or computer graphics experience: You’ll make our reconstruction process even better and easier to use, and you’ll make the final results look stunningly photorealistic.

text:
Airware is opening a technology development office in San Francisco in addition to our existing Newport Beach pad.

Who we are: Airware is redefining the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) industry, aka drone industry, by creating an operating system and development platform for small commercial UAVs. Previous solutions have been closed black boxes, while Airware’s enterprise solution combines autopilot hardware, flexible software architectures, and an API for customization and expansion. We are a rapidly growing startup, well-funded by two of the world’s pre-eminent technology venture capital firms, Andreessen Horowitz, Google Ventures, and of course YC.

Airware’s platform is currently enabling customers to tailor UAVs towards any commercial or civil application. These applications are almost unlimited: imagine building a system that helps protect endangered species in Africa from the threat of poachers, or one that allows first responders to get a nearly instant live bird’s-eye view of a disaster zone. At Airware, our engineers work every day with our customers and partners to make such visions a reality.

What it’s like to work here: The culture at Airware is unique and characterized by a diversity of individuals: Here you will find the computer hacker, private pilot, laid-back surfer, RC hobbyist, and video game designer. We work hard--really hard--but we always have a lot of fun. We take company trips, get together for boat cruises in Newport Harbor and enjoy catered lunches at the office. We are a small but growing company, and we spurn the bureaucracy that can stifle innovation and creativity. text:
MakeGamesWithUs needs a Graphic/Game Designer.

You must be an expert in both Photoshop and Illustrator. You need to be able to generate UI elements from scratch - buttons, navigation bars, HUDs, etc...

We're looking for someone to do pre-production and be 'The Finisher' of all of our games. Pre-production means mocking up the layout/flow of all the static (menus) and near-static (HUD in gameplay) elements of a game before an artist starts illustrating. Being 'The Finisher' means you will be taking near-final work from our artists and working with our producer and the developer of each game to make a completed product, ready for the App Store. This will include doing final layout of menus and HUDs, filling in missing assets (usually by modifying existing ones) where necessary, and designing screenshots to show off the game on the App Store.

We have 17 games on the App Store, many in need of tweaking immediately, and tons more in the pipeline that are getting ready to release over the coming months. In your down time you will be creating assets for social media, our website, posters, biz cards, t-shirts, etc...

Big pluses: Mobile game or app experience App icon design experience App screenshot design experience Game character design experience Game animation experience Experience creating bitmap fonts Experience creating particle effects

We need to hire immediately. Remote is a slight possibility, but ideally we need you to be in the Bay Area or be able to get here at a moments notice (we can provide housing for you if you are coming from outside of the area). You will be working out of our hacker house in Palo Alto - this is what it looks like with a bunch of our summer interns around: https://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.262781033863020.1073741828.130007087140416&type=3.

This could be a full time job for the right person or could be contract work until it is clear that you are right for the job/we are the right fit for you.

If interested email art@makegameswith.us.

title: Help us rethink commercial banking
text:
Opportunity

Standard Treasury builds software for banks. That might seem boring, but everyone uses a bank and everyone agrees bank software is crappy. Think about your online banking system with its outdated, unpleasant UI and UX — we’re working to fix that. To get some idea of the market: U.S. banks spend $400 billion dollar per year on IT.

See http://techcrunch.com/2013/07/09/standard-treasury/ for some more information.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Product

Our first product is a white-labeled API interface and developer experience that we’ll sell to banks. Our technology enables banks to programmatically offer their services to their clients using modern, RESTful APIs. From here we plan on expanding into desktop online banking, mobile banking, and core banking (the systems that record teller transactions, and how much money everyone has in their bank accounts).

Traction

We have significant traction on our API product with several top-25 banks. The price points of these contracts range from $1 million to over $5 million per year. With these contract sizes and a growing customer base; we have an opportunity to avoid any significant equity dilution with a traditional fundraising round.

Team

We are a small team based in San Francisco focused on unsexy but incredibly valuable services that will change the face of banking and we are looking for the right people to join us. We are building a team of excellent people who work hard and don’t tolerate bullshit. We want passionate partners who share our desire to shake up banking software. We practice internal transparency a la Stripe (http://bit.ly/VSv54h) and corporate candor.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Compensation and Perks

You can expect:

1. Great benefits. Medical, vision, and dental insurance for you and your dependents.

2. Great comp. Salary and equity. Critically, we’re interested in finding the right balance for you. We know there are some people who have a greater risk appetite than others.

3. Great perks. Free lunch and dinner, snacks, a stocked fridge, laundry service, gym membership, Clipper card, house cleaning by Exec or Homejoy, and delivery errands by Postmates.

4. Great mentorship. (a) Seed investment. The two co-founders previously ran a seed fund that invested in companies from earlier YC batches. We’re very interested in giving seed funding to any Standard Treasury employee that leaves the company to found a startup after two years of great work (a la 500 Friends http://bit.ly/RGcLNs). (b) Conferences. If you’re invited to speak at a conference then we’ll pay for it.

5. Great flexibility. (a) Flexible hours. So that you can live your life. (b) Open vacation policy. We all need to recharge. We mean it — there is a two week minimum and we’ll send you home in December if we have to. (c) Paid maternity and paternity leave.

6. Great tools. Build your ideal workstations so you can have the tools you want and need. Buy the books you need or want on Amazon. Need a Kindle for your commute — get it. The corporate Amex can be used for all expenses under a standard of trust & reasonableness.

Roles

We are hiring as quickly as we can find good people in a large number of roles.

1. Platform and APIs. For those who think they can build something as beautiful and durable as Twilio, Stripe, or Facebook Connect.

2. UI, UX, and design. This will start with easy-to-use API documentation and intuitive websites. In the future it will expand into the future of online (and mobile) banking.

3. Bank integrations. Half our job is taking pre-modern internal banking systems and making them disappear for our users. This requires patience and, fortunately or unfortunately, a deep love of puzzles.

4. Systems and security. We integrate with some of the most sensitive and secure systems in the world. We need to be even better. A security breach will kill our company.

5. Define your own role. Let us know what you want to work on to disrupt banking software.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

title: ZeroCater Is Hiring Hackers

text:
Opportunity

We at Standard Treasury build software for banks. That might seem boring but almost everyone uses a banks and their software is crappy. Think about your online banking system with its outdated, unpleasant UI and UX. We're working to fix that and compete with huge bank technology vendors.To get some idea of the market: U.S. banks spend $400 billion dollar a year on IT.

See http://techcrunch.com/2013/07/09/standard-treasury/ for some more information.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Product

Our first product is a white-labeled, SAAS, API interface and developer experience for banks. Our technology enables enterprises to interface with their bank over RESTful API. From here we plan on expanding into online, mobile, and core banking.

Traction

We have significant traction on our API product with several top-25 banks. The price points of these contracts range from $1.2m to $5.6m a year. With these contract sizes and a growing customer base, we have an opportunity to avoid any significant equity dilution.

Team

We are a small team focused on unsexy but incredibly valuable work that could change the face of banking. We are looking for the right people to join us. We are building a great, competent team who can't handle bullshit. We want passionate partners who share our desire to shake up banking software. We practice internal email transperceny a la Stripe (http://bit.ly/VSv54h) and corporate transperency. We are based in San Francisco.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

Compensation and Perks

You can expect

1. Great benefits. Medical vision and dental insurance for you and dependents.

2. Great comp. Salary and equity. Critically, we’re interested in finding the right balance for you. We know there are some people who have greater risk appetite than others.

3. Great perks. We haven't set up perks yet but lunch and dinner, snacks, a stocked fridge, laundry service, clipper card, gym membership, housecleaning by exec or homejoy are all on our immediate radar.

4. Great mentorship. (a) Seed investment. The two co-founders previously ran a seed fund that invested in one YC company a batch or so. We’re very interested in setting up a seed investment program for any employees with two years of great work. A la 500 Friends (http://bit.ly/RGcLNs). (b) Conferences. If you’re invited to speak at a conference then we’ll pay for it.

5. Great flexibility. (a) Flexible hours. So that you can live your life (b) Open vacation policy. We all need to re-charge. We mean it too -- there is a two week minimum. We’ll send you home in December if we have to. (c) Paid maternity and paternity leave.

6. Great tools. Build your ideal work stations, so you can have the tools you want and need. Buy the books you need or want on Amazon. Need a kindle for you commute -- get it. The corporate Amex can be used for all expenses under a reasonableness standard.

Roles We are hiring as quickly as we can find good people in a large number of roles.

1. Platform and APIs. For those who think they can build something as beautiful and durable as Twilio, Stripe, or Facebook Connect.

2. UI, UX, and design. This will start with easy-to-use API documentation and intuitive websites. In the future it expand into the future of online (and mobile) banking.

3. Bank integrations. Half our job is taking pre-modern internal banking systems and making them disappear for our users. This requires patience and, fortunately or unfortunately, a deep love of puzzles.

4. Systems and security. We build around some of the most sensitive and secure systems in the world. We need to be even better. A security breach will kill our company.

5. Define your own. You let us know.

Email us at hiring@standardtreasury.com

title: Realtime Software Engineers - PagerDuty - Toronto
text:
- To apply please send your resume to us at jobs@pagerduty.com

As an entrepreneurial backend / systems engineer, you’re caught between two worlds. You’ve toyed with the idea of just taking a job at Google, Facebook, or one of the other established big companies. You know they have more than enough interesting problems to keep you engaged, but you have a nagging feeling that you’ll be just another cog in a multi-thousand engineer machine. You want to work at a startup, but the thought of building yet another social-this or game-mechanics-that doesn’t really appeal to you.

At PagerDuty, we’re building an alerting and incident tracking system to help IT operations groups detect and respond to issues. Startups, Fortune 500 companies, and everything in between rely on us to alert them quickly when they have operational troubles. We’ve got interesting technical problems in spades, but we’re still very much a startup. We’re looking for an engineer to help us add the features our customers are clamoring for, while helping us maintain our unsurpassed uptime record as we continue to acquire new customers and scale out our systems.

Responsibilities

Scale out our alerting platform to support our rapidly growing customer base. Design resilient services and systems that can withstand multiple failures without a sweat. Work with the rest of the team to design new features to address customer requirements. Build things quickly while maintaining the high level of reliability our users have come to rely on.

Requirements

You’ve worked on distributed and highly available systems. You’ve had experience with different system architectures, and have opinions about what works and what doesn’t. Concepts like consistency, availability, real-time dispatching, and distributed queueing aren’t merely buzzwords for you. You’ve worked on enough mission critical software to know that reliability comes from a fault-tolerant design checked by an extensive test plan. When stuff goes wrong, you know that getting the system back up is only the first step. Fixing the gaps in the design and test plan is where the real work gets done. You know your way around a RDBMS - you can design schemas, write queries, and debug index problems. You’re also familiar with some NoSQL technologies and understand their use cases. You have a broad background in Computer Science fundamentals. You know that while there might be more than one right way to do something, there’s usually an awful lot of wrong ways.

Our environment

We don’t hire based on experience with a handful of tools. Instead, we want smart, capable, and experienced people who can learn our tools quickly (and suggest new ones!) as needed. Experience with our stack is just a bonus.

Here’s what we use:

Scala Finagle Ruby / Rails MySQL Cassandra Zookeeper Percona Xtradb Cluster Linux (Ubuntu) Amazon AWS (EC2, EBS, S3) HAProxy, NGinx Postfix

Benefits

Competitive salaries and company equity Generous paid vacation (3 weeks your first year, 4 weeks afterwards), unlimited sick days, regular holidays Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plan options for you and your spouse/family Pre-tax commuter benefits, and flex spending accounts Daily catered lunches and free snacks, drinks, and beer A brand new set of shiny Apple products (laptop of your choice with 27" monitor) Weekly game nights, monthly hack days and impromptu ping-pong battles Convenient office location, close to major public transit

About PagerDuty

PagerDuty is "9-1-1 dispatch" for IT, helping operations engineers and devops resolve problems with their IT systems as quickly as possible. We’re backed by some of the Valley’s best investors, including Y Combinator and Andreessen Horowitz. We're based in San Francisco, California with a presence in Toronto, Canada. We're obsessive about reliability and ensuring that when your systems are down, the right people get notified every time. PagerDuty is used by thousands of customers globally, from Fortune 500 companies to startups, including HP, Intel, Instagram, Airbnb, Box, Microsoft, Nike, Rackspace, and GitHub. We've got ambitious plans to grow and are seeking passionate people to join our crusade against downtime. We provide a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits and opportunities for career growth. For a list of all current openings, check out our at www.pagerduty.com/jobs.

Working at Zillabyte is not for everybody. Our work centers on modeling the attributes and relationships of every company in the world. It’s like a search engine for businesses but instead of indexing keywords, we index business properties. Hence, we spend a lot of time on AI, ML and other “Big Data” type problems. We make money by helping sales & marketing folks understand who their customers are and finding more of them. We can’t guarantee a 9-5 work schedule, but we can guarantee you’ll be working on some really cool original stuff, and that you’ll work with people who genuinely care about your success.

+ Build a distributed crawler that uses PhantomJS (or similar) to extract features beyond what a simple curl-based crawler can do.

+ Invent a new machine learning algorithm that can identify patterns between our customer’s data and the rest of the world’s information.

+ Develop an intuitive JS visualization that succinctly describes the “DNA” of our customers’ customers.

+ Help develop our graph-processing framework on top of Hadoop.

+ Use a Bloom Filter to capture snapshots of the web, and alert our users when there’s an interesting change.

We strongly prefer senior engineers with at least a few years of experience. You’ll be exposed to a wide range of new technologies, and we’re really looking for people that can learn quickly and iterate.

The following positions are available:

Rails Engineer :: 2+ years experience with Ruby on Rails. Experience with AWS and/or Heroku. Familiarity with continuous deployment & production environments. BS/MS in Computer Science or similar field.

Frontend/Visualization Engineer :: Strong in CoffeeScript, D3, Backbone, jQuery. Strong in CSS3 and HTML5. Good eye for design and UX experience preferred. BS/MS in Computer Science or HCI preferred.

“Big Data” Engineer :: Strong in Hadoop, especially Cascading, Scalding, and/or PIG. Experience with AWS EC2. Chef is a plus. Strong Java and Ruby. Familiarity with AI and Machine Learning. Familiarity with compilers is a plus. BS/MS in Computer Science or similar field.

Data Scientist :: Background in Machine Learning and/or AI Systems. Strong in Java and Ruby. Production experience preferred. Familiarity with distributed systems. Hadoop a plus. MS/PhD in Computer Science, Math, or Statistics preferred.

text:
We're a 3 person product- and engineering-focused startup based in sunny SoMa in San Francisco looking for our second hire. We are all hackers (1 designer / front-end hacker, 2 full stackers). We know testing is broken - how is it that something so integral to developing great products is so damn time consuming? We are changing that by building a new way to do black-box QA, one that is automated, non-technical and simple to use.

We think developers should write their own unit tests, and we practise TDD as a company. But black-box testing (testing for regressions, functional and x-browser compatibility) is way too time consuming and technically demanding. Refactoring large 'automated' test suites is painful and inefficient, and doing manual QA (especially when several browsers are involved) is enough to make the most patient dev want to quit their job.

At the moment, the only way to get black-box coverage is by spending developer time. We think it's a waste of developer time to work on anything other than hacking on product. As devs we should be spending our time building great software, not wrangling with the complexities of outdated testing tools that are designed for a pre-continuous deployment world. We think that companies want to spend money, not developer time to get coverage, and so far the market agrees with us: we have over 400 companies waiting to use us, despite being in Alpha.

We need your help to execute on our vision of making QA simple, beautiful and accessible to all.

Us:

- Reinventing how developers test software

- Seed stage company based in SF (SoMa)

- Backed by the best investors + accelerator program in the world

- Currently 3 hackers

Our stack:

- Rails

- Postgres

- Coffeescript

- Care deeply about simplicity and elegance in interfaces and in code

title: Full stack hacker for YC S13 predictive analytics startup
text:
We’re a YC-backed startup looking to disrupt the way products are made. We’re building a platform that (1) introduces massive amounts of data to a production process currently relying heavily on guesswork and (2) enables our users to get access to products before they hit the market at a discounted price.

We’re tackling a $10b problem in the retail/manufacturing industry, and we’re working with brands that have a keen focus on design (clothing, home products, furniture, electronics, etc.). In doing this, we’re also developing a unique method of ‘subjective’ profiling based on the design interests of users over time. If Facebook is a source of one’s objective qualities (age, gender, etc.), we want to become the source of one’s subjective qualities (sense of aesthetic, lifestyle, taste in clothing, etc.).

We build fast and are obsessed with design.

Some of the things we’re working on:

1. An analytics page that can segment thousands of votes by various parameters in the most efficient way possible. Each unit of data we work with has a large number of columns that need to be manipulated on the fly.

2. Early implementation of a machine learning algorithm to detect and understand the preferential patterns of users and apply it to the core product (delivering these insights within the analytics page, serving more specific content to users).

3. Building out a well-designed content interface for designers and brands to share their stories and enhance the core product.

4. Cross-domain tool for brands to use our technology on their properties (see Stripe or Gumroad) – especially in context of e-commerce tools such as Shopify, Magento, and BigCommerce

We’re looking for someone who:

1. Has a deep interest in predictive analytics and subjective profiling

2. Cares about solving a widespread problem in a somewhat archaic industry (retail)

3. Cares deeply about well-designed products (not only our application but also the brands we choose to work with)

4. Is fluent in HTML/CSS/JavaScript, JQuery, Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL, Heroku, and AWS products

5. Has an interest in machine learning

6. Learns fast by building and deploying – we pick up languages/frameworks within a few days and ship a few days later

We haven’t launched yet, so we don’t want to reveal too much. If you’re interested, please send us an email (jobs@crowdery.com) with the subject “Crowdery HN Job Post”, and please include a resume, link to your GitHub, and your favorite snack in the email body.

title: Java and rails engineer for YC S13 financial services startup - SF
text:
We're a current-batch YC-backed social enterprise creating a new and much-needed financial service for the elderly.

Financial services companies stand to make $400b per year by retaining their baby-boomer customers and we're positioning ourselves as the killer app for that. Our team is scrappy and fresh but also includes top talent from Visa and MasterCard. Still stealth, launching into private beta in August.

We're managing four pieces of technology:

1. A rails site that provides an online banking experience that is friendly, simple, and usable. The focus is reliable, secure, well-architected, etc., but the thing that makes it excellent is simplicity and a great experience, not technical bells and whistles. Our javascript is unobtrusive in every sense.

2. An java socket-server authorization service connected directly to the credit card transaction processing backbone. It's accepting, decoding, processing, re-encoding, and responding with fixed-width records over a two-way stream. Two-byte headers and signal bits and all that. High uptime and performance requirements. This is the special sauce where everyone in the industry hears about us and is like "Whoa, they let you guys process transactions! How did you get that deal signed?"

3. A learning system to support the authorization service in detecting fraud patterns. Right now this is nascent because learning systems are built on more data than we have right now. But we'll need a fast-iterating, powerful, and sophisticated framework for modeling these transactions, and we want to bake that in early.

4. The underlying infrastructure for all this, including failovers for the authorization system, integrations for email and SMS delivery, robust testing and hooks, VPNs and all that, keeping our boxes up to the security standards legally required of financial institutions.

The ideal candidate will:

* Be a good person who cares about the social mission of the company. If you're OK with people who rip off grannies, apply for a different job. If not, your country is calling.

* Be fluent in java and ruby on rails.

* Have as many as possible of:

- Some experience in systems with higher-than-average security and uptime/reliability requirements. If you've worked in consumer finance or systems that manage money, that's a plus because you know what we're dealing with. But fine if not!

- Hardware or OS or low-level-language software experience. There will be a certain level of figuring out why two threads in the pool are writing to the socket simultaneously, etc.

- Machine learning – down the road that's going to be important, and fun. If it's an interest, passion, or area of curiosity, write to us!

- Be comfortable with fast/continuous development and release cycles and working with compile/deploy automation with some panache.

We're still stealth or we'd say more! But send us a note with a resume and link to github and we'll tell more. kai.stinchcombe@gmail.com

title: PagerDuty seek a dynamic Web Engineering Manager – San Francisco

You've thought about working for a startup, but haven't yet found a small software company that understands that "no managers -- ever" is just as much of a mistake as bloating a company with useless layers of management. • Building a great team of engineers, and leading them to make sure they can do their best work • Working with the other engineering groups, sales & marketing, and the founders to make sure that the efforts of your group remain aligned with the objectives of the company • Debugging the engineering process when things don't go according to plan, and implementing fixes where necessary

Requirements

• You've worked for 3+ years as a project manager. You've experimented with different software development methodologies, and have an opinion on what works and what doesn't. You know there is a careful balance between up front thinking and shipping stuff and seeing what happens. • You've had direct reports. You know how to hire and retain great engineers. You know how to deliver both praise and constructive criticism to your people. You've seen many kinds of "people problems," and know the importance of catching them early. • Although you might not code everyday, you are still familiar with your CS fundamentals and emerging technologies. title: 2nd hire to help revolutionize testing
text:
We're a 3 person product- and engineering-focused startup based in sunny SoMa in San Francisco looking for our second hire. We are all hackers (1 designer / front-end hacker, 2 full stackers). We know testing is broken - how is it that something so integral to developing great products is so damn time consuming? We are changing that by building a new way to do black-box QA, one that is automated, non-technical and simple to use.

We think developers should write their own unit tests, and we practise TDD as a company. But black-box testing (testing for regressions, functional and x-browser compatibility) is way too time consuming and technically demanding. Refactoring large 'automated' test suites is painful and inefficient, and doing manual QA (especially when several browsers are involved) is enough to make the most patient dev want to quit their job.

At the moment, the only way to get black-box coverage is by spending developer time. We think it's a waste of developer time to work on anything other than hacking on product. As devs we should be spending our time building great software, not wrangling with the complexities of outdated testing tools that are designed for a pre-continuous deployment world. We think that companies want to spend money, not developer time to get coverage, and so far the market agrees with us: we have over 400 companies waiting to use Rainforest, despite being in Alpha.

We need your help to execute on our vision of making QA simple, beautiful and accessible to all.

Us:

- Reinventing how developers test software

- Seed stage company based in SF (SoMa)

title: PagerDuty Seek a Heavyweight Senior Software Engineer (Web Team)
text:
You've been around the block before -- you understand this "web stuff" and have built quite the number of web apps in your time. Your co-workers come to you with their most tricky performance problems, and project managers trust your estimates with only minimal padding. Junior engineers are elated for the rest of the day after their commits pass your code review.

In fact, you do your job so well that many are surprised you haven't yet been promoted into management. You, however, know that path isn't for you. You want to continue to build features, design systems, and ship products. Someone else can worry about handling the day-to-day management tasks. At PagerDuty, we’re building an alerting and incident tracking system to help IT operations groups detect and respond to issues. Startups, Fortune 500 companies, and everything in between rely on us to alert them quickly when they have operational troubles. We’ve got interesting technical problems in spades, but we’re still very much a startup. We're looking for a senior engineer to join our Web Engineering group to help us add features and improve the performance, scalability, and security of PagerDuty's web app component.

Responsibilities

We're looking for a senior engineer who will provide technical leadership for our Web Engineering group. You will be responsible for: Mentoring junior engineers in PagerDuty's deployed technologies, our engineering standards, and the art of software engineering. Collaborating with technical leaders in PagerDuty's other engineering groups to analyze complex feature requests and suggest implementation strategies. Providing engineering input into our product planning and scheduling processes. Cultivating engineering best practices within the web group, and, in conjunction with other senior engineers, company wide.

Overseeing the design & evolution of PagerDuty's REST API (http://developer.pagerduty.com/documentation/rest). Shepherding the process of converting PagerDuty to an API + rich JS client architecture. Building & shipping features!

Requirements

You're a seasoned engineering manager -- expertly adept at managing people and projects alike. title: Head of Web Engineering - PagerDuty
text:
Head of Web Engineering - PagerDuty!

To Apply please send your resume to jobs@pagerduty.com

PagerDuty isn't your typical Bay Area startup. We actually have paying customers: thousands of them in fact. These range from established public companies (Microsoft, Nike, HP, Sony) to startups (Dropbox, Square, Yelp, AirBnB) and everything in between. Your job will be to ramp up our content production across print, web and social media to inform existing customers, educate new ones, and demonstrate our thought leadership in the IT operations space. We need someone willing to roll up their sleeves and create amazing content without being afraid to test, experiment and optimize.

At PagerDuty, we’re building an alerting and incident tracking system to help IT operations groups detect and respond to issues. Startups, Fortune 500 companies, and everything in between rely on us to alert them quickly when they have operational troubles. We’ve got interesting technical problems in spades, but we’re still very much a startup. We’re looking for an engineer to help us add the features our customers are clamoring for, while helping us maintain our unsurpassed uptime record as we continue to acquire new customers and scale out our systems.

Responsibilities

Scale out our alerting platform to support our rapidly growing customer base. Design resilient services and systems that can withstand multiple failures without a sweat. Work with the rest of the team to design new features to address customer requirements. Build things quickly while maintaining the high level of reliability our users have come to rely on.

Requirements

You’ve worked on distributed and highly available systems. You’ve had experience with different system architectures, and have opinions about what works and what doesn’t. Concepts like consistency, availability, real-time dispatching, and distributed queueing aren’t merely buzzwords for you.

You’ve worked on enough mission critical software to know that reliability comes from a fault-tolerant design checked by an extensive test plan. When stuff goes wrong, you know that getting the system back up is only the first step. Fixing the gaps in the design and test plan is where the real work gets done.

You know your way around a RDBMS — you can design schemas, write queries, and debug index problems. You’re also familiar with some NoSQL technologies and understand their use cases.

You have a broad background in Computer Science fundamentals. You know that while there might be more than one right way to do something, there’s usually an awful lot of wrong ways.

Our Environment

We don’t hire based on experience with a handful of tools. Instead, we want smart, capable, and experienced people who can learn our tools quickly (and suggest new ones!) as needed. Experience with our stack is just a bonus.

Here’s what we use:

Scala Finagle Ruby / Rails MySQL Cassandra Zookeeper Percona Xtradb Cluster Linux (Ubuntu) Amazon AWS (EC2, EBS, S3) HAProxy, NGinx Postfix

Benefits

Competitive salaries and company equity Generous paid vacation (3 weeks your first year, 4 weeks afterwards), unlimited sick days, regular holidays Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plan options for you and your spouse/family Pre-tax commuter benefits, and flex spending accounts Daily catered lunches and free snacks, drinks, and beer A brand new set of shiny Apple products (laptop of your choice with 27" monitor) Weekly game nights, monthly hack days and impromptu ping-pong battles Convenient office location, close to major public transit

About PagerDuty

PagerDuty is "9-1-1 dispatch" for IT, helping operations engineers and devops resolve problems with their IT systems as quickly as possible. We’re backed by some of the Valley’s best investors, including Y Combinator and Andreessen Horowitz. We're based in San Francisco, California with a presence in Toronto, Canada. We're obsessive about reliability and ensuring that when your systems are down, the right people get notified every time. PagerDuty is used by thousands of customers globally, from Fortune 500 companies to startups, including HP, Intel and GitHub. We've got ambitious plans to grow and are seeking passionate people to join our crusade against downtime. We provide a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits and opportunities for career growth. For a list of all current openings, check out our careers page at http://www.pagerduty.com/jobs/ To apply for this role please send your resume to jobs@pagerduty.com. Thank you!

title: Help grow a community of hackers
text:
Welcome to hackerrank.com where we're building an engaged community of problem solvers in different domains of CS.

Hypothesis

Every hacker has a type of challenge presented in a certain level of difficulty that really intrigues him/her. We're working to build the largest and the most engaging community of hackers.

Milestones:

We just crossed our 110k user mark and our 3-week retention is hovering around 20%. We're growing fast and... we're still in beta.

Problem

The problem with moving fast is it should be managed well, else all the effort isn't worth it. There are users who love it (https://twitter.com/GeneralBison/status/316539960129884161) and users who don't like it much (https://twitter.com/thomasABoyt/status/316030881812840448). It's easy to get this sort of feedback because they're posting it publicly. But what do we do about passive users? We're missing tons of critical pieces of information & feedback from our users which we'd like to fix.

Welcome <your-name-here>

title: Job titles, shmob titles
text:
At 42Floors we still don’t have traditional job titles. As our company has grown, we keep attracting more entrepreneurs who themselves have never cared about job titles. We’re now at 14 people, and we still don’t really have any hierarchy in the company; so there is not really a need to embrace a lot of formal organization.

A little while ago, we did implement some processes to keep creative anarchy and functional teamwork in balance. But hierarchy and job titles still didn’t emerge.

In fact, the only reason we have job titles on our open positions is that the rest of the world kind of expects them; but once you get here, we don’t really care. We’re a startup. Everyone wears multiple hats. Smart people will do awesome stuff if given the freedom to figure it out.

We’d love for you to come check us out. If you want to write Ruby or Backbone.js, or manage a sales pipeline or talk commercial real estate, we might have a job title that’s right for you.

title: You don’t have to know anything about commercial real estate
text:
In fact, we prefer if you don’t.

At 42Floors, we’re making it easier to search for office space. In the last year, we have launched our search site in San Francisco and New York. We’ve helped 1,000+ companies find 2 million+ square feet of office space. We’ve raised $17M from industry leaders.

And all of this has been done by a bunch of people that know almost nothing about commercial real estate. In fact, the first seven people in the company had never done any commercial real estate work at all before starting 42Floors.

But we like that. Because we’re not trying to make this industry a little bit better, we’re totally flipping it on its head. Believe it or not, commercial real estate as an entire industry has still not undergone even the most simple of internet transformations. Right now, in 2013, you can’t search for commercial real estate online. It’s crazy actually.

To actually transform this industry, we need people who are not educated in how the industry has performed up until now. In fact, the actual skill you need is the skill of transformation. Of revolution. Of being able to see the world in a totally different light. We look for people who aren’t confined by what has been, as if it’s all that could ever be. We look for people that have the confidence (and at times blind faith) to believe that transparency will eventually win.

If you want to work for us and know absolutely nothing about commercial real estate, that’s actually good thing. For now.

Once you get the job, you don’t get to stay naïve. You have to be willing to work hard. You have to enjoy learning for learning’s sake. That means talking to tenants, brokers, and landlords. That means going on tours and reading leases. You can get up to speed quickly, if you work at it. We know, because that’s what each one of us had to do when we started.

It’s invigorating to learn about an entirely new industry. To see nothing but opportunity everywhere you look. People like us are drawn to problems. Hard problems. Actually, it’s a bit of an addiction. And we have the audacity to think we can accomplish anything.

It’s time to come talk to us. We need more people like you.

http://42floors.com/jobs

text:
Heap is an entirely new approach to analytics: just capture everything, and organize it all after-the-fact. This lets our customers conduct powerful analytics without having to ship code or wait for data.

It works. We're profitable and revenues are growing sharply, just a few weeks after launch.

There are 3 fundamental pillars to our product:

1) Real-time infrastructure. Our problem statement is slightly ridiculous. We need to embed ourselves in every app session, pipe each action up to our servers, slice and dice the data in arbitrary ways, and serve the results in sub-second latencies. All in real-time.

2) Data capture. We automatically capture client-side actions on web. But there are other platforms we can hook into. And other types of data we can capture. We’ve expanded the search space of user data considerably, but there’s far more that needs to be done.

3) Data visualization. With the volume of data Heap consumes, simple pre-generated graphs just don't cut it. There's an exponential increase in the number of ways to organize the data, and a need for proactively separating signal from noise.

We need help on all these fronts. We’re venture-backed and very generous with compensation.

Email jobs@heapanalytics.com for more info.

title: Come help us hack the Auto Industry - Dealer Sales
text:
It's not often you'll find a job post on HN for a sales role, but we think every discipline has its hackers. As a Dealer Sales Executive at CarWoo!, you'll be responsible for selling our products to car dealerships.

You'll have to hack each dealership's org chart to win and be successful in this role.

Here's what you'll be challenged to do:

1. Find a way to get the potential customer on the phone. Dealers are inundated with phone calls and you have to figure out how to get them to spend a few minutes of their time with you. Good hackers (sales) will find a way.

2. Once you get them on the phone, quickly analyze if they are a sales target and triage them into your priority target list. Wasting time on targets who aren't willing or don't have a need to buy is like an endless while loop in software. You'll need to find the most optimized path to achieving success while avoiding endless while loops.

3. When you find a great sales target, help them find success selling cars using a new platform (we have a free version of our product). We find that our most successful sales people are also the most knowledgable about or product, have technical acumen and can earn the trust of our dealers by helping them find success using our products.

3. After you've won over the end user, find a way to sell the decision maker. No easy answer here, you'll have to navigate the org chart at each of your targets and find, convince and sell the decision maker.

4. Support your sold customers and ensure they are extremely happy with the product they purchased. You'll have some help here as we have a team of dedicated Performance Managers who manage the day to day success of our customers, but you'll be required to check in from time to time and make sure they have everything they need.

I call this hacking because good sales people can see the inefficiencies, weaknesses and opportunities in a system and find a way to use them to their advantage.

Requirements

* A willingness to try something new and challenge yourself to hack a different kind of system.

* Desire to be a part of an awesome culture, make good money and change an industry.

* Have a desire to overcome your insecurities and challenge yourself to get outside of your comfort zone.

* Desire to have part of your pay tied to your performance. The more you can sell, the more you can make.

Bonus Points

* Experience in sales a plus, but not a requirement.

* Experience working with car dealerships.

Full medical, dental, vision and life insurance.

title: DevOps Engineer at Scribd: Help run one of the largest Rails sites, SF or Remote
text:
Scribd is building the world’s online library of books and documents. We’re one of the top 100 sites on the web by traffic, but our ops team is still just three people. As one of the first rails sites to reach scale, we’ve already built a lot of specialized infrastructure to make our business possible, but we have a lot more to do.

Scribd has an agile, startup culture and an unusually close working relationship between engineering and ops. You’ll regularly find cross-over work at Scribd, with ops people writing application-layer code. We think we’re able to make that work because of the uniquely talented people we have on the team.

To allow us to keep scaling, we’re looking to add an experienced DevOps engineer to our small team. As a member of Scribd operations, you’ll have tremendous ownership and responsibility for the site and its infrastructure.

This role is open to remote employees working from anywhere in the world. Let us know when you apply if you want to work remotely or would be interested in relocating to San Francisco. We are happy to support either.

What you’ll do

- Expand/improve/fix a 150+ growing server farm and infrastructure which is running on top of it - Build new back-end infrastructure using ruby and chef - Support the engineering team by building awesome internal tools for developers - Keep Scribd.com up and fast - Be a part of 24x7 on-call schedule with other members of the DevOps team

Some things we’ve built

There is a lot of technology operating behind the scenes at Scribd. We’ve built the first HTML5 document reader, a multi-terabyte data warehouse, a resizing image CDN, and a remote-controlled go-kart (really!)

For more, see our jobs page (scribd.com/jobs) and tech blog (coding.scribd.com)

You should have

- Strong general programming skills - Related experience with website operations; this includes experience with high volume/high traffic web sites - Strong oral and written communication skills - Strong knowledge of most widely-used networking protocols and unix/linux command line tools - Solid scripting skills

Even better would be ...

- 3+ Years of solid Linux/UNIX systems engineer/administrator experience - Hands-on experience with building and maintaining reliable large-scale distributed systems environments - Experience with ruby, rails, and chef - Excellent database knowledge, particularly with MySQL - HBase/Hadoop deployment/scaling/maintaining experience - Experience with any of the following technologies/tools: Nginx, HAProxy, Memcached, Squid, git, Solr, Sphinx, Hive, ActiveMQ, Postfix, Tomcat, Jetty, Glassfish, Redis

To apply We're easy to reach. Just send your resume and cover letter with the subject “[Your name] – DevOps Engineer [SF or remote] – via Hacker News” to jobs@scribd.com.

Your application will be reviewed by a senior member of our engineering team within 24 hours.

title: MobileWorks is hiring a star Community Operations Manager
text:
Join Us!

MobileWorks is reinventing crowdsourcing, and we’re looking for enthusiastic, passionate, and fun individuals to join our team. We’re a venture-backed company with a central social mission: using technology as a source of economic empowerment for underemployed and marginalized individuals around the world. If you are excited about how crowdsourcing is changing the way the world does work, then MobileWorks is the place for you.

About the position:

We’re experiencing fantastic growth and need an all-star community operations manager to interface with the MobileWorker community and our clients to keep things running smoothly. You’ll be working on our Premier product, which provides hands-on, direct assistance to our highest-value clients.

At MobileWorks, you’ll have the opportunity to work with a diverse range of community members from around the world to ensure that we continue to provide fantastic service. You’ll make sure that each client using Premier has an incredible experience, not just through direct customer service, but also by building design processes and policies that support Premier as we add hundreds of new staffers and clients each month.

You’re a self-motivated, detail-oriented person that loves managing projects with a lot of moving parts. Bringing people together--perhaps with a wide variety of backgrounds--is second nature to you. Great communication is something you take personal pride in--it’s not just a bullet point to check off on an application. You take great satisfaction in training others on a team to be successful with their roles. You get jazzed knowing that you brought a group together to complete a well-done project. * 1-2 years of experience in an operations management, community management, customer service, or similar role in a startup or small company * Experience training or teaching others new skills * Killer (in a good way) communications skills * Worked with people from a wide variety of backgrounds (international experience a huge plus!) * Are extremely service oriented * Super savvy with new technology * Have tried Premier and can tell us what you think about it!

Why work at MobileWorks? Just a few reasons...

* The chance to work with a bright, fun team on an impact product * Competitive salary and stock options * Full health coverage * Paid gym membership * Unlimited paid vacation days * The workspace setup of your choice (chair, monitor, choice of computer) * Breathtaking sunset views of the Golden Gate Bridge from your desk

text:
Manager, Customer Service Operations

About You

Customer service is more than a job for you. It's a way of life. You get a thrill out of making customers happy, and seeing your team do the same. You're driven and you always get the job done, but you have a playful side and know when to laugh with your team, build camaraderie, and get them excited about the mission they are on. You can switch contexts quickly. One minute, you're going the extra mile to thrill a customer, the next, you're diving into a spreadsheet to analyze operations and see where you need to improve.

You are looking for a group of passionate people who share your vision for what customer service should be. You're looking for the flexibility to be quirky and fun as you really wow customers. You're ready to sign up for a mission where you will play a key role in redefining an industry.

About CarWoo!

Located in Silicon Valley, CarWoo! is a game-changing Internet company dedicated to providing the best online buying and selling platform for car shoppers and the dealers who service them. Transparency and great customer service are at the center of our mission. In the CarWoo! MarketPlace, consumers can select the type of car they are interested in, find and communicate anonymously with dealers, compare offers, and ultimately make a confident purchase decision. Dealers have the opportunity to receive never before available competitive intelligence and insight into the behavior of qualified, online buyers. CarWoo! is expanding its business every day and has been featured on The View, The Today Show, CNN Money, and other leading national media outlets.

Learn more about CarWoo at http://carwoo.com/about

Job Description

You will run the CarWoo! Customer Happiness team, and report directly to our COO. You will define, implement, and optimize all call center and online communication policies. You will help your people grow and learn and improve; resolve conflicts; ensure work product consistently meets established standards, and generally be there to make sure the ship is sailing smoothly.

Lots of feedback from customers will get thrown at you, and it will be up to you to organize that feedback and work closely with the Product Team to define and implement product improvements, including admin tools and applications. You will rely on extensive operational and call center experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals.

Measures of success for this role shall include, but not be limited to: Time to first response for service tickets Time to resolution for service tickets Customer (consumer and dealer) satisfaction scores Ensuring 3 dealer offers are made to consumers (deal satisfaction rate) New dealership and salesperson signups Dealer subscription package upsells Net promoter scores for the CarWoo! service

Duties*

Above all else, provide amazing customer support to CarWoo! Users via phone, chat, email, and text Recruit, hire, motivate, and mentor Customer Happiness Reps Manage call team potentially as large as 10+ people Develop training programs for new hires and when implementing process or product changes Schedule employee shifts, managing for anticipated spikes and lulls in traffic Clearly identify metrics / key performance indicators to measure employee productivity relative to goals for performance reviews Perform statistical analysis on volumes of outbound and inbound calls, new consumers, dealer offers, satisfied (3 or more offers) and unsatisfied (less than 3 offers) deals, and other key metrics Define and advocate for product changes that improve operational efficiency Translate dealer and customer feedback into cogent feature/functional recommendations Support Dealer Sales team to maximize team performance (exceed quotas, maximize consumer engagements, minimize dealer attrition)

Qualifications and Skills

Must have 3-5+ years experience in call center operations management and personnel management with a special focus on outbound call centers Familiarity with call center operation work flows Basic understanding of dealer sales department workflows is a plus Strong communication, leadership and management skills. Demonstrated and proven ability to recruit, hire, train and retain effective outbound call center agents Ability to analyze statistics and define operational efficiencies as they pertain to call center operations Comfortable with analytics tools including spreadsheets and databases Eagerness to work in a rapidly growing start-up environment Outgoing, persuasive, success-oriented personality College degree (or substantial equivalent life experience) Compensation *Salary plus bonus based on achieving and exceeding quarterly goals

Email rudi@carwoo.com if you are interested, and tell us why you're a good fit. In the subject line, write "Customer Happiness Manager"

title: Help Scale Rescale (YC W12)

• BS in Computer Science or equivalent

• Solid developer with experience building scalable and maintainable systems.

• Opinionated about the art of building software but not a jerk about it.

• Familiarity with cloud computing architecture, particularly AWS.

Nice to Have:

• Experience in any of the following languages and frameworks (the more the better): Java, Hadoop, Python, Django, Knockout, Javascript

• Experience scaling and tuning both relational and non-relational databases.

• Experience with HPC, particularly MPI.

==========

Interested? Contact us at jobs@rescale.com

title: MakeGamesWithUs (YC W12) is hiring an iOS Game Dev
text:
About us:

We teach people (primarily high school and college kids) how to build iPhone games. Our site (http://www.makegameswith.us) contains project based tutorials which culminate in building a clone of Angry Birds. After completing the tutorials, developers get started making their own original game. We also provide a toolkit to speed up development of games, along with forums to enable developers to show off their progress and get help. Once their game is nearly ready, we skin the game with professional art, and finally publish and promote the games for a share of the revenue. You can check out our first 10 games here (http://www.mgw.us).

We're currently a team of 4 who live and work out of a 4500 sqft house in Palo Alto, it would be awesome if you're willing to move in with us, although living elsewhere in the Bay Area works too. We're a young team with a relaxed work environment, and we love our work so we tend to do it most of the time. When we're not working we're throwing a big party or just kicking back and playing fifa or super smash brothers. We also take the occasional company trip for a change of scenery, our last one was to France, and our next will be to New Orleans.

We are striving to build a big gaming business while inspiring people to explore computer science and learn to build complete products. We're well funded by Y Combinator and undisclosed top tier VCs/angels. It's a great opportunity to join an early stage startup on the ground floor and work with a young and dedicated team.
